# Steal a Brainrot (SAB) fact sheet for the MASSAB riddle mode.
# This is the Roblox game, not Fortnite's "Steal the Brainrot" map. Promo codes appear only in "Codes and promotions", each with a dated status, and no code there is claimed to work today.
# Researched on 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05, and expanded on 2026-11-06. "As of November 2026" means the value was read from the cited page on those dates.
# Lines in "Upcoming and unreleased content" are teasers and leaks, not confirmed releases, and they go stale quickly.
# Lines about Sammy use the word Sammy as well as SpyderSammy, because the matcher treats them as different words.
# Income and cost numbers change when the developer buffs or nerfs a Brainrot, so older guides often show other numbers.
# Rule for fact lines: a value stays in a fact line only if the sources read agree on it, or one credible source states it and nothing contradicts it.
# Credible here means the Roblox API, Sportskeeda, Beebom, Dexerto, PocketGamer.biz, Story Kitchen, Wikipedia, and the Steal a Brainrot Fandom wiki (community run).
# If sources are split with no clear majority, the disputed value is left out of the fact line and every side is in Needs review.
# If a clear majority agrees against one stray or weak page, the fact keeps the majority value and the disagreement is still in Needs review.
# Weak pages are SEO or marketplace blogs such as rblxguide, u7buy, Eldorado, Playgama, Finding Dulcinea and The Game of Nerds.
# Sportskeeda's www pages block automated fetches, so their text was read from the hindi3.sportskeeda.com copy of the same article. The www URLs cited here were opened in a browser to confirm they load.
# Lines added on 2026-11-06 carry extra fields inside the source tag, which the matcher strips along with it: id, type (official, secondary or community), status (confirmed, corroborated or unverified), confidence, pub (when the source was published), event (when it happened), checked (when it was verified) and note.
# status: confirmed means a primary source or two independent reputable sources, corroborated means two independent sources, unverified means one source or community only. Fields with no known value are left out.
# Also treated as credible from 2026-11-06: Roblox's shareholder letter on sec.gov, playsab.com, Guinness World Records, GamesRadar, TechWiser, IGN, Know Your Meme, Insider Gaming and Pocket Tactics.
# Lines in "Brainrot stats" were generated by script from each page's wiki infobox, so they are only as current as the wiki.
# Expanded again on 2026-11-07 by one research agent per category. Those lines carry checked=2026-11-07 and an id
# whose prefix names the category: C01 Sammy, C02 updates, C03 roster, C04 mechanics, C05 items and places,
# C06 events, C07 riddles and codes, C08 meme origins, C09 machines, C10 records and business, C11 Lucky Blocks
# and rituals, C12 relationships, C13 limited Brainrots, C14 monetization, C15 sounds and secrets, and B1 to B8
# for per-Brainrot wiki pages. Every new line's evidence was machine-checked against the cited page; lines whose
# evidence or numbers did not match are in Needs review instead.

## What each brainrot is

# Each line says what a Brainrot is and its rarity. Rarities and looks come from the Fandom wiki as read on 2026-11-05.
# The first lines repeat the best known Brainrots in Wikipedia's words, since those are the words a riddle answer is likely to use.

Tralalero Tralala is a three-legged shark wearing Nike sneakers. [source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_brainrot]
Tung Tung Tung Sahur is made of wood, a wooden log holding a wooden bat. [source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_brainrot]
Bombardiro Crocodilo has the head of a crocodile and the body of a World War II bomber plane. [source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_brainrot]
Ballerina Cappuccina is a ballerina with a cappuccino mug for a head. [source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_brainrot]
Lirilì Larilà, also written Lirili Larila, is a cactus elephant wearing sandals. [source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_brainrot]
Chimpanzini Bananini is a chimpanzee with a banana for a body. [source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_brainrot]
Trippi Troppi is a cat with a shrimp's body. [source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_brainrot]

## Game overview

Steal a Brainrot is a Roblox game published by the Roblox group BRAZILIAN SPYDER. [source: https://games.roblox.com/v1/games?universeIds=7709344486]
The release date of Steal a Brainrot is May 15, 2025: the game came out and launched on Roblox that day, so it released in May 2025 on the 15th. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Steal_a_Brainrot_(Game) | status=confirmed | checked=2026-11-08 | also=https://knowyourmeme.com/memes/subcultures/steal-a-brainrot , https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Update_0 | note=Sammy's riddle answer FISHINOCLOWNINO15 gives day 15, and Know Your Meme and the Fandom game and Update 0 pages say May 15, 2025. Wikipedia's May 16 is the UTC date of the Roblox record, made at 00:49 UTC.]
Steal a Brainrot launched on Roblox in May 2025. [source: https://www.story-kitchen.com/news/story-kitchen-partnering-with-steal-a-brainrot-creators-on-feature-adaptation-of-roblox-game]
The official Roblox record for Steal a Brainrot shows the experience was created at 00:49 UTC on May 16, 2025, which was still May 15, 2025 in US time. [source: https://games.roblox.com/v1/games?universeIds=7709344486]
Steal a Brainrot servers hold a maximum of 8 players. [source: https://games.roblox.com/v1/games?universeIds=7709344486]
Roblox files Steal a Brainrot under the Simulation genre and the Tycoon subgenre. [source: https://games.roblox.com/v1/games?universeIds=7709344486]
The official description of Steal a Brainrot tells players to buy a Brainrot, steal Brainrots from other players, generate money, rebirth, and buy slaps and troll gear. [source: https://games.roblox.com/v1/games?universeIds=7709344486]
The official description of Steal a Brainrot credits Chris for letting the game use the Nyan Cat and WinnersTakesAll for the backpack system. [source: https://games.roblox.com/v1/games?universeIds=7709344486]
The Brainrots in Steal a Brainrot are characters based on the 2025 Italian brainrot memes. [source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steal_a_Brainrot]
The gameplay loop of Steal a Brainrot has been compared to capture the flag. [source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steal_a_Brainrot]
Steal a Brainrot gets a new update every Saturday, usually at 3 PM EST, and an Admin Abuse of about 30 to 60 minutes follows it. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Admin_Abuse]
The latest Steal a Brainrot update as of early November 2026 is Update 73 on October 31, 2026, with Update 74 listed for November 7, 2026. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Update_Log]
The Steal a Brainrot Fandom wiki counts 557 indexable Brainrots as of November 2026, or 571 with Lucky Blocks and other miscellaneous entries. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Brainrots]
Steal a Brainrot's Roblox record had 15,504,929 upvotes and 2,708,823 downvotes as of November 6, 2026. [source: https://games.roblox.com/v1/games/votes?universeIds=7709344486 | id=A02-0005 | type=official | status=confirmed | confidence=high | checked=2026-11-06 | note=Vote counts from the Roblox votes API, a snapshot taken on November 6, 2026.]
As of November 6, 2026, Steal a Brainrot sells three Roblox game passes: Admin Commands for 7,999 Robux, VIP for 375 Robux, and 2x Money for 299 Robux. [source: https://apis.roblox.com/game-passes/v1/universes/7709344486/game-passes?passView=Full&pageSize=100 | id=A02-0006 | type=official | status=confirmed | confidence=high | checked=2026-11-06 | note=All three passes are listed for sale in the Roblox game-pass API, with no further pages. Prices can change.]

## Machines

The fuse-style machines in Steal a Brainrot released in this order: Fuse Machine (August 2025), Witch Fuse (October 2025), Santa's Fuse (December 2025), Divine Fuse (March 2026), Summer Fuse (May 2026), Haunted Fuse (October 2026). [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Update_Log]
The Rainbow Machine was the first machine in Steal a Brainrot, added in June 2025 (June 21, 2025); players deposited 25 Gold Brainrots to start a 15-minute Rainbow event. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Rainbow_Machine]
The Bubblegum Machine in Steal a Brainrot was added in July 2025 (July 18, 2025), needed 10 Candy Brainrots, and was the first trait machine. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Bubblegum_Machine]
The first Fuse Machine in Steal a Brainrot released in August 2025 (August 1, 2025). [source: https://www.sportskeeda.com/roblox-news/steal-brainrot-fuse-machine-update-patch-notes]
The first Fuse Machine in Steal a Brainrot followed the Bubblegum Machine and stood next to the Coin Shop. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Fuse_Machine]
The Fuse Machine in Steal a Brainrot takes 4 Brainrots plus cash, and the cost and wait depend on the rarity of the Brainrots submitted. [source: https://www.sportskeeda.com/roblox-news/steal-brainrot-fuse-machine-update-patch-notes]
At launch the Steal a Brainrot Fuse Machine offered 12 Brainrots including 2 Secrets, Agarrini la Palini and Los Combinasionas. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Update_Log/Update_10]
The Steal a Brainrot Fuse Machine waits 15 minutes when the rarest input is Common, Rare or Epic, 30 minutes for Legendary, Mythic or Brainrot God, and 1 hour 30 minutes for Secret or OG. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Fuse_Machine]
Players could reveal a Steal a Brainrot Fuse Machine result early for 299 Robux. [source: https://beebom.com/steal-a-brainrot-fuse-machine-guide]
The first Fuse Machine in Steal a Brainrot was removed in September 2025 (September 6, 2025) and replaced by the Craft Machine. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Fuse_Machine]
The Fuse Machine returned to Steal a Brainrot in January 2026 (January 24, 2026 at 3 PM EST) and the Divine Fuse later replaced it. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Fuse_Machine]
The Craft Machine in Steal a Brainrot released in September 2025 (September 6, 2025) with Update 15 and replaced the Fuse Machine. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Update_Log/Update_15]
Each Steal a Brainrot Craft Machine recipe uses 4 Brainrots, and the craftable options change every 30 minutes. [source: https://techwiser.com/steal-a-brainrot-craft-machine-how-use-guide/]
The Craft Machine in Steal a Brainrot was removed in October 2025 (October 11, 2025 at 3 PM EST) and replaced by the Witch Fuse. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Craft_Machine]
The Craft Machine returned to Steal a Brainrot in September 2026 (September 12, 2026) with Update 66. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Update_Log/Update_66]
The Witch Fuse in Steal a Brainrot released in October 2025 (October 11, 2025 at 3 PM EST) and the Brainrot Dealer replaced it in November 2025 (November 8, 2025). [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Witch_Fuse]
The Witch Fuse in Steal a Brainrot is a Halloween cauldron next to the Shop that accepts any 4 Brainrots and uses cash to start the fusion. [source: https://www.sportskeeda.com/roblox-news/steal-brainrot-witch-fuse-guide]
Headless Horseman was the highest-income Brainrot in the Steal a Brainrot Witch Fuse at $175M/s when Sportskeeda's guide was written in October 2025. [source: https://www.sportskeeda.com/roblox-news/steal-brainrot-witch-fuse-guide]
The Witch Fuse in Steal a Brainrot introduced the rule that mixed inputs give a Brainrot one rarity below the highest input, and it cut the chance of inheriting traits and mutations from 10-20% to 5-15%. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Witch_Fuse]
The Brainrot Dealer in Steal a Brainrot replaced the Witch Fuse in November 2025 (November 8, 2025), restocked Brainrots every 30 minutes, and was dropped after player complaints. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Brainrot_Dealer]
The Brainrot Trader in Steal a Brainrot replaced the Brainrot Dealer in November 2025 (November 15, 2025) and offered four trades every two hours. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Brainrot_Trader]
The Admin Machine in Steal a Brainrot was added in November 2025 (November 29, 2025) and removed in December 2025 (December 13, 2025). [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Admin_Machine]
Santa's Fuse in Steal a Brainrot released in December 2025 and replaced the Brainrot Trader in the lobby. [source: https://www.sportskeeda.com/roblox-news/steal-brainrot-santa-s-fuse-machine-guide]
Santa's Fuse in Steal a Brainrot takes four Brainrots and gives limited-time Christmas Brainrots, and a Brainrot made in it cannot be fused again. [source: https://www.sportskeeda.com/roblox-news/steal-brainrot-santa-s-fuse-machine-guide]
The Duels Machine in Steal a Brainrot lets two players wager one Brainrot each and fight in a private server, and the winner takes the other Brainrot. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Duels_Machine]
The Trade Machine in Steal a Brainrot released in February 2026 and lets players send trade requests in their server and across servers. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Update_Log/Update_39]
The Divine Fuse in Steal a Brainrot released in March 2026 (March 7, 2026) with Update 41 and replaced the original Fuse Machine. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Update_Log/Update_41]
Sammy leaked the Steal a Brainrot Divine Fuse on February 28, 2026 during an Admin Abuse, and the community picked it in a poll over bringing back the OG Craft Machine. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Divine_Fuse]
The Divine Fuse in Steal a Brainrot was later replaced by the Cyber Craft Machine. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Divine_Fuse]
Griffin is the top Divine Fuse Brainrot in Steal a Brainrot, with an income of $400M/s. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Griffin]
The Cyber Craft Machine in Steal a Brainrot released in April 2026 (April 18, 2026) with Update 47 and launched with 11 Brainrots. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Update_Log/Update_47]
The Summer Fuse in Steal a Brainrot released in May 2026 (May 23, 2026) with Update 52 and holds 19 Brainrots. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Summer_Fuse]
Dragon Aquanini is the top Summer Fuse Brainrot in Steal a Brainrot, with an income of $375M/s. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Summer_Fuse]
The Summer Fuse in Steal a Brainrot was removed in August 2026 (August 1, 2026) with Update 60. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Update_Log/Update_60]
Los Traders in Steal a Brainrot released in July 2026 (July 11, 2026) and refreshes its trade offers every 30 minutes. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Update_Log/Update_57]
Los Traders was removed from Steal a Brainrot in August 2026 (August 8, 2026) when the RNG Machine arrived. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Update_Log/Update_61]
The RNG Machine in Steal a Brainrot released in August 2026 (August 8, 2026) as a luck-based machine with Legendary to Secret Brainrots and upgrades tied to rebirths. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/RNG_Machine]
The Taco Merchant in Steal a Brainrot appeared for one hour on the August 18, 2026 Taco Tuesday and sold Burrito Bat, Tacoturbo Tacorito, Nachorilla, and Sammyni Truckini for tacos. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Taco_Merchant]
The Headless Merchant in Steal a Brainrot ran from October 31 to November 1, 2026 and sold Brainrots for Candy Corns from the Trick or Treat event. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Headless_Merchant]
The Haunted Fuse in Steal a Brainrot released in October 2026 (October 3, 2026) with Update 69, replaced the Craft Machine, and looks like a haunted house. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Haunted_Fuse]

## Events and Admin Abuse

Admin Abuse in Steal a Brainrot is a special event where a host such as Sammy, Steak, or Caylus uses admin powers to spawn rare Brainrots, raise luck, and run server-wide events. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Admin_Abuse]
Sammy often gives an early bird present, usually a Secret Lucky Block, to Steal a Brainrot players who are online about one hour before an Admin Abuse. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Admin_Abuse]
The Bloodmoon Event in Steal a Brainrot lasted 15 minutes, spawned every 3 hours, and is listed by the Fandom wiki as the first event in the game. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Update_Log/Update_02]
Taco Tuesday in Steal a Brainrot is a weekly Admin Abuse event hosted by the developer every Tuesday. [source: https://www.sportskeeda.com/roblox-news/when-is-taco-tuesday-steal-a-brainrot]
The Taco event in Steal a Brainrot is one of the game's earliest events and gives random Brainrots the Taco trait from a cannon above the conveyor belt entrance. [source: https://www.sportskeeda.com/roblox-news/steal-brainrot-taco-event-guide]
The Taco trait in Steal a Brainrot gives a 3x income multiplier and puts a taco on the Brainrot's head. [source: https://www.sportskeeda.com/roblox-news/steal-brainrot-taco-event-guide]
The Raining Tacos song plays when the Steal a Brainrot Taco Tuesday event opens. [source: https://www.sportskeeda.com/roblox-news/when-is-taco-tuesday-steal-a-brainrot]
Taco Lucky Blocks and Los Taco Blocks spawn on the conveyor belt during Steal a Brainrot Taco Tuesday, and a Los Taco Block costs $300,000,000. [source: https://www.sportskeeda.com/roblox-news/when-is-taco-tuesday-steal-a-brainrot]
Fat Sammy in Steal a Brainrot is a Taco Tuesday NPC next to the Robux Shop who takes 10 Brainrots with the Taco trait, down from 15 at launch. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Taco_Tuesday]
Fat Sammy's reward odds in Steal a Brainrot are Tipi Topi Taco 75%, Capi Taco 12.5%, Bombardini Tortinii 10%, and Nooo My Hotspot 2.5%. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Fat_Sammy]
Tacorita Bicicleta was added on the September 16, 2025 Taco Tuesday in Steal a Brainrot as a limited Brainrot with a stock of one million. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Taco_Tuesday]
The Extinct Event in Steal a Brainrot spawned 1 of 3 limited Brainrots on the Red Carpet every 2 hours. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Update_Log/Update_16]
The Witching Hour event in Steal a Brainrot ran every two hours and spawned Vampira Cappucina, Zombie Tralala, Frankentteo, or La Vacca Jacko Linterino on the conveyor belt. [source: https://www.sportskeeda.com/roblox-news/steal-brainrot-witch-fuse-guide]
The Winter Hour event in Steal a Brainrot ran every two hours for 3 to 4 minutes and gave Brainrots the Santa Hat trait. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Update_Log/Update_28]
The Turkey Event in Steal a Brainrot ran around Thanksgiving 2025 and spawned Gobblino Uniciclino on the map, which players had to hit 10 times. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Turkey_Event]
The Bruno Mars concert in Steal a Brainrot took place on January 17, 2026, lasted just under eight minutes, was pre-recorded, and featured five identical Bruno Mars avatars. [source: https://www.dexerto.com/roblox/steal-a-brainrots-bruno-mars-concert-hits-12-7-million-concurrent-players-3305913/]
The Escape Tsunami limited time mode in Steal a Brainrot was added on January 24, 2026 and removed on April 4, 2026. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Escape_Tsunami_LTM]
Stealing was disabled in the Steal a Brainrot Escape Tsunami limited time mode. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Update_Log/Update_35]
The Backrooms Event in Steal a Brainrot runs every 2 hours on weekdays and every hour on weekends, and Evil Sammy entities guard it. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Backrooms_Event]
The Jump for Eggs limited time mode in Steal a Brainrot has players jump between islands to collect eggs and earn XP on trampolines to unlock new islands. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Jump_for_Eggs_LTM]
The Event Board that ran the Halloween event traits in Steal a Brainrot was removed on November 2, 2025 at 11:00 AM EST. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Events | id=A05-0014 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | event=2025-11-02 | checked=2026-11-06 | note=The Events page does not name the board in this row; the Halloween page gives the same removal time for the Halloween traits.] [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Halloween | checked=2026-11-06]
The New Year's Machine in Steal a Brainrot was added on December 31, 2025 at 12 PM EST. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/New_Year%27s_Machine | id=A05-0022 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | event=2025-12-31 | checked=2026-11-06]
The Easter Event Board in Steal a Brainrot was added on April 4, 2026 at 3 PM EST with Easter Part 2. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Easter_Eventboard | id=A05-0032 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | event=2026-04-04 | checked=2026-11-06]
The John Pork event in Steal a Brainrot was released on May 2, 2026 at 3 PM EST. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/John_Pork_Event | id=A05-0039 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | event=2026-05-02 | checked=2026-11-06]
The Spain Event in Steal a Brainrot started on July 25, 2026 and added the Spain trait. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Spain_Event | id=A05-0051 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | event=2026-07-25 | checked=2026-11-06]
Fortunu and Cashuru is the rarest Brainrot obtainable from the Leprechaun Lucky Block in Steal a Brainrot. ## Rebirths

Rebirth in Steal a Brainrot takes the required Brainrots and most of your money, and gives new gear, a higher multiplier, and usually more base slots. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Rebirth]
Steal a Brainrot has 19 rebirths as of November 2026, and each one adds 10 seconds to the Lock Base time. [source: https://beebom.com/steal-a-brainrot-rebirth-guide-levels-and-rewards/]
Rebirth 1 is the only Steal a Brainrot rebirth that does not add a base slot. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Rebirth]
Before Update 66 a Steal a Brainrot rebirth took every Brainrot in your base; since then it takes only the required Brainrots. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Rebirth]
Rebirth 1 in Steal a Brainrot costs $500K and requires Trippi Troppi and Gangster Footera; it unlocks the Friend Controller, Iron Slap, Gravity Coil, and Bee Launcher. [source: https://beebom.com/steal-a-brainrot-rebirth-guide-levels-and-rewards/]
Rebirth 1 in Steal a Brainrot used to require Tung Tung Tung Sahur until Gangster Footera replaced it after the character's removal. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Rebirth]
Rebirth 2 in Steal a Brainrot costs $1.5M and requires Brr Brr Patapim and Boneca Ambalabu; it unlocks Gold Slap, Coil Combo, Rage Table, and the second base floor. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Rebirth]
Rebirth 3 in Steal a Brainrot costs $12.5M and requires Trulimero Trulicina and Chimpanzini Bananini; it unlocks Diamond Slap, Grapple Hook, and Taser Gun. [source: https://beebom.com/steal-a-brainrot-rebirth-guide-levels-and-rewards/]
Rebirth 4 in Steal a Brainrot costs $35M and requires Chef Crabracadabra and Glorbo Fruttodrillo; it unlocks Emerald Slap, Invisibility Cloak, and Boogie Bomb. [source: https://beebom.com/steal-a-brainrot-rebirth-guide-levels-and-rewards/]
Rebirth 5 in Steal a Brainrot costs $100M and requires Frigo Camelo and Orangutini Ananassini; it unlocks Ruby Slap and Medusa's Head. [source: https://beebom.com/steal-a-brainrot-rebirth-guide-levels-and-rewards/]
Rebirth 6 in Steal a Brainrot costs $350M and requires Bombardiro Crocodilo; it unlocks Dark Matter Slap and Web Slinger. [source: https://beebom.com/steal-a-brainrot-rebirth-guide-levels-and-rewards/]
Rebirth 7 in Steal a Brainrot costs $1B and requires Bombombini Gusini; it unlocks Flame Slap, Quantum Cloner, and All Seeing Sentry. [source: https://beebom.com/steal-a-brainrot-rebirth-guide-levels-and-rewards/]
Rebirth 8 in Steal a Brainrot costs $5B and requires Te Te Te Sahur; it unlocks Nuclear Slap and Rainbowrath Sword. [source: https://beebom.com/steal-a-brainrot-rebirth-guide-levels-and-rewards/]
Rebirth 9 in Steal a Brainrot costs $12.5B and requires Cocofanto Elefanto; it unlocks Galaxy Slap and Laser Cape. [source: https://beebom.com/steal-a-brainrot-rebirth-guide-levels-and-rewards/]
Rebirth 10 in Steal a Brainrot costs $125B and requires Girafa Celestre; it unlocks Glitched Slap, Body Swap Potion, and the third base floor. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Rebirth]
Rebirth 11 in Steal a Brainrot costs $800B and requires Tralalero Tralala; it unlocks Splatter Slap and Paintball Gun. [source: https://beebom.com/steal-a-brainrot-rebirth-guide-levels-and-rewards/]
Rebirth 12 in Steal a Brainrot costs $3.5T and requires Odin Din Din Dun; it unlocks Heart Balloon and Magnet. [source: https://beebom.com/steal-a-brainrot-rebirth-guide-levels-and-rewards/]
Rebirth 13 in Steal a Brainrot requires Trenostruzzo Turbo 3000 and unlocks Megaphone and BeeHive. [source: https://beebom.com/steal-a-brainrot-rebirth-guide-levels-and-rewards/]
Rebirth 14 in Steal a Brainrot costs $40T and requires Trippi Troppi Troppa Trippa; it unlocks Gummy Bear and Subspace Mine. [source: https://beebom.com/steal-a-brainrot-rebirth-guide-levels-and-rewards/]
Rebirth 15 in Steal a Brainrot costs $100T and requires Pakrahmatmamat; it unlocks Heatseeker. [source: https://beebom.com/steal-a-brainrot-rebirth-guide-levels-and-rewards/]
Rebirth 16 in Steal a Brainrot requires the Secret Brainrot Los Tralaleritos and unlocks Attack Doge, and it is the first rebirth to require a Secret. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Rebirth]
Rebirth 17 in Steal a Brainrot requires Job Job Job Sahur and Chicleteira Bicicleteira and unlocks Giant Potion. [source: https://beebom.com/steal-a-brainrot-rebirth-guide-levels-and-rewards/]
Rebirth 18 in Steal a Brainrot costs $10Qa and requires Graipuss Medussi; it unlocks Flash Teleport. [source: https://beebom.com/steal-a-brainrot-rebirth-guide-levels-and-rewards/]
Rebirth 19 in Steal a Brainrot costs $30Qa and requires La Grande Combinasion. [source: https://beebom.com/steal-a-brainrot-rebirth-guide-levels-and-rewards/]
Rebirth 19 in Steal a Brainrot raised the base from 27 to 28 slots. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Update_Log/Update_62]
Rebirth 16 in Steal a Brainrot requires 1Qa ($1 quadrillion) in cash and Los Tralaleritos in the base. ## Bases, stealing and trading

The base in Steal a Brainrot stores your Brainrots, which generate cash over time, and it can have up to 3 floors. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Base]
The first floor of a Steal a Brainrot base has 10 slots, Rebirth 2 unlocks the second floor, and Rebirth 10 unlocks the third floor. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Base]
The Lock Base in Steal a Brainrot starts at 60 seconds, gains 10 seconds per rebirth, and gains a fixed 10 seconds with the VIP gamepass. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Base]
The Red Carpet in Steal a Brainrot, also called the Conveyor Belt, is where Brainrots walk across the map to be bought. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Red_Carpet]
A Brainrot bought from the Steal a Brainrot Red Carpet can be bought by another player while it walks to the base for 150% of its base cost. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Red_Carpet]
When a Brainrot is being stolen in Steal a Brainrot, the base owner gets a message and an alarm sound. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Stealing]
A player carrying a stolen Brainrot in Steal a Brainrot cannot use gears, and their speed drops from 34 to 20 and their jump height from 7.2 to 4.32. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Stealing]
The Steal a Brainrot steal message uses the rarity color: green Common, blue Rare, purple Epic, yellow Legendary, red Mythic, rainbow Brainrot God, black and white Secret, black and yellow OG. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Stealing]
The Steal a Brainrot Index gives a +0.5x base multiplier for completing the Default, Gold, Diamond, or Rainbow Index, which each need 75% of the game's Brainrots. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Index]
The Trade Plaza in Steal a Brainrot is a place where stealing is disabled and has three sections: the normal plaza, the Pro plaza (25B/s), and the OG plaza (100B/s and an OG Brainrot). [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Trading_Plaza]
Lucky Blocks in Steal a Brainrot can be bought and stolen like Brainrots, do not generate money, and open into a random Brainrot. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Lucky_Blocks]
The Secret Lucky Block in Steal a Brainrot costs $750M. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Secret_Lucky_Block]
Los Lucky Blocks in Steal a Brainrot are exclusive to Admin Abuse and cost $250,000,000 on the conveyor. [source: https://www.sportskeeda.com/roblox-news/steal-brainrot-rebirth-16-update-guide]
Offline cash in Steal a Brainrot stops accumulating 5 hours after the player's last in-game session. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Offline_Cash | id=A04-0011 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-06 | note=Only the Fandom wiki states this cap; no independent source was found. The offline rate is disputed (see the offline cash rate conflict).]
In Steal a Brainrot, the Like Goal Milestone spawned a random Brainrot God each time the game reached another 100,000 likes, and it could not run in private servers. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Like_Goal_Milestone | id=A04-0014 | type=community | status=corroborated | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-06 | note=Fandom describes the milestone in the past tense, and it may no longer run. The corroborating Allthings guide (August 2026) mentions Brainrot God spawns at like milestones.] [source: https://allthings.how/steal-a-brainrot-roblox-efficient-stealing-events-and-rebirths | checked=2026-11-06]
In Steal a Brainrot, Brainrot God and Secret spawns on the Red Carpet are announced only in the player's own server, while OG spawns are also shown in the Live Spawns panel. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Red_Carpet | id=A04-0015 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-06]

## Mutations and traits

A Brainrot in Steal a Brainrot can have only one Mutation but any number of Traits. [source: https://www.sportskeeda.com/roblox-news/steal-brainrot-all-traits-multipliers]
The Steal a Brainrot Mutation multipliers include Gold 1.25x, Diamond 1.5x, Bloodrot 2x, Candy 4x, Lava 6x, Yin Yang 7.5x, Radioactive 8.5x, Cursed 9x, Rainbow 10x, Divine 10x, Cyber 11x, Phantom 12x, and Crystal 13x. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Mutations]
Gold and Diamond were the first mutations in Steal a Brainrot, added in May 2025 (May 31, 2025). [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Mutations]
The Gold mutation in Steal a Brainrot has a 10% chance on the Red Carpet, Diamond has 5%, and Rainbow has 1%. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Mutations]
The Rainbow mutation in Steal a Brainrot was added in June 2025 (June 21, 2025) and gives a 10x multiplier. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Mutations]
The Bloodrot mutation in Steal a Brainrot gives a 2x multiplier and comes from the Bloodmoon event. [source: https://www.sportskeeda.com/roblox-news/all-mutations-effects-steal-brainrot]
The Candy mutation in Steal a Brainrot was added in July 2025 (July 5, 2025) and gives a 4x multiplier during the Candy Aurora event. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Mutations]
The Lava mutation in Steal a Brainrot was added in July 2025 (July 25, 2025) and gives a 6x multiplier during the Molten event. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Mutations]
The Galaxy mutation in Steal a Brainrot was added in August 2025 (August 23, 2025) and comes from the Galactic event. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Mutations]
The Yin Yang mutation in Steal a Brainrot was added in September 2025 (September 27, 2025) and gives a 7.5x multiplier. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Mutations]
The Radioactive mutation in Steal a Brainrot was added in November 2025 (November 15, 2025) and gives an 8.5x multiplier. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Mutations]
The Cursed mutation in Steal a Brainrot was added in January 2026 (January 3, 2026) and gives a 9x multiplier. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Mutations]
The Divine mutation in Steal a Brainrot was added in February 2026 (February 21, 2026), gives a 10x multiplier, and can also give the Halo trait. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Mutations]
The Cyber mutation in Steal a Brainrot was added in April 2026 (April 18, 2026) and gives an 11x multiplier. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Mutations]
The Phantom mutation in Steal a Brainrot was added in June 2026 (June 13, 2026) and gives a 12x multiplier. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Mutations]
The Crystal mutation in Steal a Brainrot was added in July 2026 (July 25, 2026) and gives a 13x multiplier. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Mutations]
The Eclipse mutation in Steal a Brainrot was added in October 2026, is listed as the best mutation, and was called Celestial before release. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Eclipse_Event]
The Celestial mutation in Steal a Brainrot gave a 4x multiplier and could only be activated by the developer as of June 2026. [source: https://www.sportskeeda.com/roblox-news/all-mutations-effects-steal-brainrot]
Collecting 75% of the Brainrots in one mutation unlocks that mutation's base skin in Steal a Brainrot. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Mutations]
Beebom and the Fandom wiki both treat Steal a Brainrot mutation and trait multipliers as additive, so a Lava mutation (6x) with a Bombardiro trait (4x) gives 10x. [source: https://beebom.com/steal-a-brainrot-mutations-and-traits-list]
Traits in Steal a Brainrot can come from developer events, player rituals, or weather, and a Brainrot can hold any number of them. [source: https://www.sportskeeda.com/roblox-news/steal-brainrot-all-traits-multipliers]
The Taco trait in Steal a Brainrot gives 3x, the Concert trait 5x, the Crab trait 5x, the Paint trait 6x, the Nyan trait 6x, the Meowl trait 7x, and the Strawberry trait 8x. [source: https://www.sportskeeda.com/roblox-news/steal-brainrot-all-traits-multipliers]
The Strawberry trait in Steal a Brainrot only appears when a Strawberry Elephant spawns on a server. [source: https://www.sportskeeda.com/roblox-news/steal-brainrot-all-traits-multipliers]
The Sleepy trait is the only Steal a Brainrot trait that lowers income. [source: https://www.sportskeeda.com/roblox-news/steal-brainrot-all-traits-multipliers]
The Galaxy mutation in Steal a Brainrot gives a 7x multiplier as of November 2026. ## Rarities and common Brainrots

Steal a Brainrot has eight rarities, from lowest to highest: Common, Rare, Epic, Legendary, Mythic, Brainrot God, Secret, and OG. [source: https://beebom.com/all-brainrots-in-steal-a-brainrot/amp/]
The Secret rarity was added to Steal a Brainrot in May 2025 (May 31, 2025) with Update 1. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Update_Log/Update_01]
The OG rarity was added to Steal a Brainrot in August 2025 (August 30, 2025) with Update 14 and is rarer than Secret. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Update_Log/Update_14]
OG is the rarest class in Steal a Brainrot, and every OG except Headless Horseman has its own event when it spawns. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/OG]
Secret is the second-best rarity in Steal a Brainrot, with 270 Brainrots as of November 2026 and a spawn chance below 0.001%. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Secret]
The name of a Brainrot God is said out loud when it spawns in Steal a Brainrot. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Brainrot_God]
Noobini Pizzanini is a Common Brainrot in Steal a Brainrot that costs $25 and makes $1/s. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Noobini_Pizzanini]
The Common Brainrots in Steal a Brainrot include Noobini Pizzanini, Lirili Larila, Tim Cheese, FluriFlura, Talpa Di Fero, Svinina Bombardino, Pipi Kiwi, and Pipi Corni. [source: https://beebom.com/all-brainrots-in-steal-a-brainrot/amp/]
The Rare Brainrots in Steal a Brainrot include Trippi Troppi, Gangster Footera, Bandito Bobritto, Boneca Ambalabu, Cacto Hipopotamo, Ta Ta Ta Ta Sahur, and Tric Trac Baraboom. [source: https://beebom.com/all-brainrots-in-steal-a-brainrot/amp/]
The Epic Brainrots in Steal a Brainrot include Cappuccino Assassino, Brr Brr Patapim, Trulimero Trulicina, Bambini Crostini, Bananita Dolphinita, and Perochello Lemonchello. [source: https://beebom.com/all-brainrots-in-steal-a-brainrot/amp/]
The Legendary Brainrots in Steal a Brainrot include Burbaloni Loliloli, Ballerina Cappuccina, Chef Crabracadabra, Lionel Cactuseli, Glorbo Fruttodrillo, and Sigma Boy. [source: https://beebom.com/all-brainrots-in-steal-a-brainrot/amp/]
The Mythic Brainrots in Steal a Brainrot include Frigo Camelo, Orangutini Ananassini, Rhino Toasterino, Bombardiro Crocodilo, Bombombini Gusini, and Te Te Te Sahur. [source: https://beebom.com/all-brainrots-in-steal-a-brainrot/amp/]
The Brainrot God Brainrots in Steal a Brainrot include Girafa Celestre, Matteo, Tralalero Tralala, Odin Din Din Dun, Trenostruzzo Turbo 3000, and Trippi Troppi Troppa Trippa. [source: https://beebom.com/all-brainrots-in-steal-a-brainrot/amp/]

## OG Brainrots

The OG Brainrots in Steal a Brainrot as of November 2026 are Skibidi Toilet, John Pork, Headless Horseman, Meowl, Strawberry Elephant, and Spyder Elephant. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/OG]
Strawberry Elephant is the first OG Brainrot in Steal a Brainrot, released in August 2025 (August 30, 2025) with Update 14. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Strawberry_Elephant]
Strawberry Elephant in Steal a Brainrot costs $750B and has an income of $750M/s as of November 2026, up from $250M/s when it released. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Strawberry_Elephant]
Strawberry Elephant was first made in 2007 by a user named mzic2403 for a Photoshop competition, according to the Steal a Brainrot Fandom wiki. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Strawberry_Elephant]
Meowl is the second OG Brainrot added to Steal a Brainrot, released in October 2025 (October 18, 2025) with Update 21. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Meowl]
Meowl in Steal a Brainrot has an income of $600M/s and costs $650B as of November 2026. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Meowl]
Skibidi Toilet is the third OG Brainrot added to Steal a Brainrot, released in December 2025 (December 27, 2025) with Update 31. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Update_Log/Update_31]
Skibidi Toilet in Steal a Brainrot has an income of $450M/s and costs $450B as of November 2026, the lowest income of any OG. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Skibidi_Toilet]
Headless Horseman was added to Steal a Brainrot in October 2025 (October 25, 2025) as a Witch Fuse Secret and became an OG in Update 40 in February 2026. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Headless_Horseman]
John Pork is an OG Brainrot added to Steal a Brainrot in May 2026 (May 2, 2026) with Update 49, costing $500B with an income of $500M/s. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/John_Pork]
Spyder Elephant is an OG Brainrot released in Steal a Brainrot in May 2026 with Update 51, with an income of $1B/s and a cost of $1T. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Spyder_Elephant]

## Rituals

Rituals in Steal a Brainrot are secret easter eggs activated by using specific Brainrots in a specific pattern, and the Brainrots used are permanently deleted. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Rituals]
The La Vacca ritual in Steal a Brainrot uses 3 La Vacca Saturno Saturnita held in a triangle and spawns Las Vaquitas Saturnitas. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Rituals]
The Spiderini ritual in Steal a Brainrot uses four Sammyni Spyderini in a square and gives Los Spyderinis. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Update_Log/Update_14]
The Chicleteira Bicicleteira ritual in Steal a Brainrot uses 2 Chicleteira Bicicleteira on the two sides of the Red Carpet and spawns Los Chicleteiras. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Update_Log/Update_16]
The Karkerkar ritual in Steal a Brainrot needs four players each holding Karkerkar Kurkur in a diamond shape, and it lets you buy Los Karkeritos for $200,000,000. [source: https://www.sportskeeda.com/roblox-news/steal-brainrot-rebirth-16-update-guide]
The 1x1x1x1 ritual in Steal a Brainrot uses 4 Guerriro Digitale in a diamond shape in the tube behind the Brainrot Spawner and gives 1x1x1x1 at 99.5% or Guest 666 at 0.5%. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Update_Log/Update_23]
The Job Job Job Sahur ritual in Steal a Brainrot uses four Job Job Job Sahur lined up in the Shop and gives Yess my Resume at 99% or Noo my Resume at 1%. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Update_Log/Update_60]
The Money Money Puggy ritual in Steal a Brainrot uses 2 Money Money Puggy to get Los Puggies. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Update_Log/Update_65]

## Developer, studio and legal

SpyderSammy, display name Sammy, owns the Roblox group BRAZILIAN SPYDER that publishes Steal a Brainrot. [source: https://groups.roblox.com/v1/groups/35815907]
The BRAZILIAN SPYDER Roblox group behind Steal a Brainrot had about 39.5 million members on November 4, 2026. [source: https://groups.roblox.com/v1/groups/35815907]
Wikipedia credits Steal a Brainrot to Sammy (SpyderSammy) and says DoBig Studios owns the game. [source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steal_a_Brainrot]
Sammy (SpyderSammy), the Steal a Brainrot developer, is a chief officer at Do Big Studios. [source: https://roblox.fandom.com/wiki/Player:SpyderSammy]
Sammy (SpyderSammy), the Steal a Brainrot developer, started in game development in 2013 and also worked on Blade Ball, Race Clicker, Schedule, and Fisch. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/SpyderSammy]
A Steal a Brainrot movie was announced in January 2026 (January 29, 2026), with Story Kitchen developing and producing it with Do Big Studios and Spyder Games. [source: https://www.dexerto.com/roblox/robloxs-steal-a-brainrot-is-being-adapted-into-a-movie-3311810/]
The Steal a Brainrot movie was in early development with no release date when it was announced. [source: https://www.dexerto.com/roblox/robloxs-steal-a-brainrot-is-being-adapted-into-a-movie-3311810/]
The Steal a Brainrot movie is led by Dmitri M. Johnson, Michael Lawrence Goldberg, Timothy I. Stevenson, and Elena Sandoval, with Think Influence producing in association. [source: https://www.story-kitchen.com/news/story-kitchen-partnering-with-steal-a-brainrot-creators-on-feature-adaptation-of-roblox-game]
Tung Tung Tung Sahur was removed from Steal a Brainrot in September 2025 amid licensing talks over the character. [source: https://www.dexerto.com/gaming/steal-a-brainrot-mascot-disappears-from-roblox-after-copyright-dispute-3252146/]
Tung Tung Tung Sahur returned to Steal a Brainrot in November 2025 (November 29, 2025) and was removed again in April 2026 (Update 48). [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Update_Log/Update_48]
In October 2025 Spyder Games and Speedy Simulator Gaming sued the creator of the Fortnite Creative map Stealing Brainrots, an unlicensed copy of Steal a Brainrot, for alleged copyright infringement. [source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steal_a_Brainrot] [source: https://insider-gaming.com/steal-a-brainrot-developers-sue-fortnite-copycat/ | id=A15-0017 | type=secondary | checked=2026-11-06]
Epic Games licensed Steal a Brainrot for Fortnite Creative as Steal the Brainrot, released in July 2025, which is a separate game from the Roblox original. [source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steal_a_Brainrot]
Steal a Brainrot won Best Creative Direction at the 2025 Roblox Innovation Awards, presented at RDC 2025. [source: https://beebom.com/roblox-innovation-awards-2025-winners]
The Star reported in March 2026 that Steal a Brainrot is made by Spyder Games, based in Louisiana, and Speedy Simulator Gaming, based in Wyoming. [source: https://www.thestar.com.my/tech/tech-news/2026/03/25/robloxs-hit-game-steal-a-brainrot-battles-its-many-imitators]
Spyder Games and Speedy Simulator Gaming, the companies behind Steal a Brainrot, had filed at least four lawsuits against alleged imitators by March 2026. [source: https://www.thestar.com.my/tech/tech-news/2026/03/25/robloxs-hit-game-steal-a-brainrot-battles-its-many-imitators]
Steal a Brainrot had earned an estimated US$64 million from in-game purchases by March 2026, according to Romonitor data cited by The Star. [source: https://www.thestar.com.my/tech/tech-news/2026/03/25/robloxs-hit-game-steal-a-brainrot-battles-its-many-imitators]
Adam Starr, general counsel at Do Big Studios, told GamesBeat in February 2026 that the company was trying to bring Steal a Brainrot to the big screen. [source: https://gamesbeat.com/roblox-creators-view-film-and-tv-adaptations-as-a-promising-revenue-stream/]
Mementum Lab SAS, a French company, sent a cease-and-desist over Tung Tung Sahur to Steal a Brainrot in September 2025. [source: https://www.dexerto.com/roblox/tung-tung-sahur-is-at-the-center-of-a-bizarre-federal-custody-battle-over-brainrot-characters-3381733/]
The companies behind Steal a Brainrot sued Mementum Lab in the US District Court for the Northern District of California, arguing that Tung Tung Sahur was AI-generated and has no valid copyright. [source: https://www.dexerto.com/roblox/tung-tung-sahur-is-at-the-center-of-a-bizarre-federal-custody-battle-over-brainrot-characters-3381733/]
A hearing in the Steal a Brainrot case against Mementum Lab was set for September 16, 2026, no judge had ruled on the core questions as of Dexerto's July 2026 report, and searches on November 6, 2026 found no report of a ruling. [source: https://www.dexerto.com/roblox/tung-tung-sahur-is-at-the-center-of-a-bizarre-federal-custody-battle-over-brainrot-characters-3381733/]
Steal a Brainrot has also been released on Meta Horizon for VR. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Steal_a_Brainrot_(Game)]
The BRAZILIAN SPYDER group behind Steal a Brainrot was created on April 1, 2025. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/BRAZILIAN_SPYDER]
do_small is a Brazilian Roblox developer, the co-creator of Steal a Brainrot, and a former Chief Operations Officer of Do Big Studios. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Do_Small]
The Fandom wiki lists do_big as the CEO of Do Big Studios, the company connected to Steal a Brainrot. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Do_Small]
The Steal a Brainrot management team on the Fandom wiki lists SpyderSammy, do_small as co-owner, Atavi as QA Lead, and Guga as Game Producer. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/BRAZILIAN_SPYDER]
The official Steal a Brainrot accounts are StealaBrainrotR on X and YouTube and stealabrainrotdevs on TikTok. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/BRAZILIAN_SPYDER]
Do Big Studios' official website describes its offer to game developers as full acquisitions, minority investments, and operating partnerships. [source: https://www.dobigstudios.com/ | id=A01-0004 | type=official | status=confirmed | confidence=high | checked=2026-11-06 | note=The official site does not mention Steal a Brainrot on the pages read, so the game is not listed as a Do Big title there.]

## Sammy, the owner

Sammy, whose Roblox username is SpyderSammy, created Steal a Brainrot with do_small under the group BRAZILIAN SPYDER. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Steal_a_Brainrot_(Game)]
The Star's March 2026 report names Sammy (SpyderSammy), the Steal a Brainrot developer, as Sam Brakta. [source: https://www.thestar.com.my/tech/tech-news/2026/03/25/robloxs-hit-game-steal-a-brainrot-battles-its-many-imitators]
Sammy said Steal a Brainrot was inspired by Steal a Character, a game whose rights he acquired and improved. [source: https://www.thestar.com.my/tech/tech-news/2026/03/25/robloxs-hit-game-steal-a-brainrot-battles-its-many-imitators]
Sammy, the Steal a Brainrot owner, wrote on X: "I've been making games on ROBLOX since 2013." [source: https://www.eldorado.gg/blog/sammy-steal-a-brainrot-guide/]
Sammy's first original Roblox project before Steal a Brainrot was Crab Game, made in 2022 under the Spyder Games group. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/SpyderSammy]
After Crab Game, Sammy made Mining Clicker Simulator under the Spyder Crew group, before Steal a Brainrot. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/SpyderSammy]
Sammy, the Steal a Brainrot owner, joined the Blade Ball team as a lead developer in late 2023. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/SpyderSammy]
Sammy, the Steal a Brainrot owner, released Pixel Tower Defense in 2024 under the Red Spyder group, and it was discontinued in April 2025 after more than 26 million visits. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/SpyderSammy]
Sammy, the Steal a Brainrot owner, released Line to Riches in early 2025 under the Blue Spyder group, a game for gathering donations with more than 15.6 million visits. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/SpyderSammy]
The Roblox wiki also lists Sammy, the Steal a Brainrot owner, as a developer on Blue Lock: Rivals, DIG, Build A Plane, Steal a Car, TCG Card Shop Simulator, and Line to Fight. [source: https://roblox.fandom.com/wiki/Player:SpyderSammy]
Sammy, the Steal a Brainrot owner, posts as SpyderSammy on X, spydersammy on TikTok, and spydersammy333 on Instagram. [source: https://www.eldorado.gg/blog/sammy-steal-a-brainrot-guide/]
Sammy is most active on the official Steal a Brainrot Discord, especially the bombardiro-news channel. [source: https://www.eldorado.gg/blog/sammy-steal-a-brainrot-guide/]
The Fandom wiki lists the United States as the country of Sammy, the Steal a Brainrot owner. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/SpyderSammy]
The Fandom wiki gives the birthday of Sammy, the Steal a Brainrot owner, as February 25. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/SpyderSammy]
Sammy always says ":3" during Steal a Brainrot Admin Abuses. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/SpyderSammy]
Sammy's Steal a Brainrot catchphrases include "I spoil y'all way too much", "someone said La Vacca?", "one more snap?", and "raining lucky block?". [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/SpyderSammy]
Sammy's favorite Brainrot in Steal a Brainrot is Meowl, which he said in the community server's Exclusive Chat. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/SpyderSammy]
Sammy's Roblox avatar is red themed, and red represented his team in the Steal a Brainrot Admin Abuse War. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/SpyderSammy]
Jandel mocked Sammy as "Scammy Sammy" during the Steal a Brainrot Admin Abuse War, and detractors still use the nickname. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/SpyderSammy]
Sammy usually mentions having tacos for dinner and often eats them during Steal a Brainrot Taco Tuesday. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Admin_Abuse]
Sammy's Snap in Steal a Brainrot is an animation where Sammy runs down the Red Carpet with a red aura and snaps, which starts almost all in-game events at once. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Admin_Abuse]
The Coffin Snap in Steal a Brainrot is Sammy's Snap with Sammy coming out of a coffin first. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Admin_Abuse]
Raining Lucky Blocks is what Sammy calls spawning a large number of Lucky Blocks at once during a Steal a Brainrot Admin Abuse. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Admin_Abuse]
Random Server Spawns let Sammy spawn a chosen Brainrot in a set number of Steal a Brainrot servers. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Admin_Abuse]
Sammy runs Secret Admin Abuses in Steal a Brainrot mostly on Sundays and Friday nights, sometimes opening with "is anyone there". [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Admin_Abuse]
Sammy's Base in Steal a Brainrot is an event first activated during the Admin Abuse War on August 23, 2025, with Brainrot God and Secret Brainrots inside. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Sammy%27s_Base]
Sammy's Base in Steal a Brainrot floats in the sky and has a small table with tacos and a chair, but it does not show Sammy's real base. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Admin_Abuse]
Sammy spawned La Karkerkar Combinasion by mistake on the September 9, 2025 Steal a Brainrot Taco Tuesday and then nerfed it. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Admin_Abuse]
Sammy added Raccooni Jandelini to Steal a Brainrot before the Admin Abuse War to poke fun at Jandel, the creator of Grow a Garden. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Admin_Abuse]
Jandel, the owner of Grow a Garden, started the Admin Abuse War against Sammy and Steal a Brainrot on August 23, 2025, accusing Sammy of stealing ideas. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Admin_Abuse_War]
Grow a Garden won the Admin Abuse War against Sammy's Steal a Brainrot on player count. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Admin_Abuse]
During the Admin Abuse War, Sammy said Admin Abuse existed in Blox Fruits first, and Blox Fruits creator mygame43 appeared in Steal a Brainrot. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Admin_Abuse_War]
Sammy took a 3-week break to work on the Steal a Brainrot Summer Update, and Steak became the first YouTuber to host an Admin Abuse. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Steak%27s_Admin_Abuse]
Steak's Steal a Brainrot Admin Abuse was meant to be hosted by Caylus, but Sammy let Steak host it instead. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Steak%27s_Admin_Abuse]
Sari, a YouTuber listed from Japan, hosted a Secret Admin Abuse in Steal a Brainrot for Japan and has a personal snap. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Sari]
The Steal a Brainrot Brainrots based on Sammy include Sammyni Spyderini, Sammyni Fattini, Sammyni Cakini, Sammyni Truckini, and Sammyni Spookyni. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Sammy_(Disambiguation)]
Spyder Elephant in Steal a Brainrot was created by Sammy, has Strawberry Elephant's look covered in diamonds, and comes from the Spyder Chain sold in Spyder Simulators. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Spyder_Elephant]
Spyder Elephant is the first unstealable Brainrot in Steal a Brainrot and the first OG obtainable with Robux. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Spyder_Elephant]
Sammy added polls to Steal a Brainrot on the February 17, 2026 Taco Tuesday, and the poll made Headless Horseman an OG. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Poll]
Sammy said on the April 7, 2026 Steal a Brainrot Taco Tuesday that adding an OG is slow because it needs permission from the meme's creator. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/OG]
Skibidi Toilet was teased for Steal a Brainrot on September 20, 2025 and released after a collaboration with Invisible Narratives, which owns the IP. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/OG]
A hacked developer spawned Rainbow Headless Horsemen in all Steal a Brainrot servers on October 22, 2026, and the game was shut down for about an hour. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Steal_a_Brainrot_(Game)]
Sammy said he would "make an example out of" the person behind the October 22, 2026 Steal a Brainrot hack. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Steal_a_Brainrot_(Game)]
A person using the alias John Doe breached Steal a Brainrot on March 18, 2026 and posted messages such as "W JANDEL" while Sammy was offline. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/John_Doe_Hacking]
SpyderSammy's official X profile, @SpyderSammy, describes Sammy as a game producer. [source: https://x.com/SpyderSammy | id=A01-0001 | type=official | status=confirmed | confidence=high | checked=2026-11-06 | note=Read on 2026-11-06 from the X profile page.]
SpyderSammy's X account, @SpyderSammy, was created in April 2021. [source: https://x.com/SpyderSammy | id=A01-0002 | type=official | status=confirmed | confidence=high | event=2021-04 | checked=2026-11-06]
Crab Game, SpyderSammy's first original Roblox game, was closed in August 2022 and has been unplayable since then, as of November 2026. [source: https://roblox.fandom.com/wiki/Player:SpyderSammy | id=A01-0005 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | event=2022-08 | checked=2026-11-06 | note=Only the Roblox wiki gives this; the Steal a Brainrot wiki says the game was made in 2022.] [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/SpyderSammy | checked=2026-11-06]
SpyderSammy joined the Wiggity. development team as a lead developer for Blade Ball in late 2023. [source: https://roblox.fandom.com/wiki/Player:SpyderSammy | id=A01-0006 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | event=2023-12 | checked=2026-11-06 | note=The Steal a Brainrot wiki says he joined the Blade Ball team in late 2023 without naming Wiggity. This adds the team name only from the Roblox wiki.] [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/SpyderSammy | checked=2026-11-06]

## Upcoming and unreleased content

Steal a Brainrot Update 74 is listed for November 7, 2026, and its content had not been announced as of November 5, 2026. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Update_Log/Update_74]
Smurf Cat is an upcoming OG Brainrot in Steal a Brainrot with no release date as of November 2026. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Smurf_Cat]
Sammy hinted at Smurf Cat for Steal a Brainrot at the September 27, 2025 Admin Abuse by saying "y'all DONT believe the OGs im planning" and sending mushroom and cat emojis. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Smurf_Cat]
Sammy also hinted at Smurf Cat for Steal a Brainrot by saying "hopefully the next base skin is a blue with a mushroom on top". [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Smurf_Cat]
Smurf Cat, the upcoming Steal a Brainrot OG, was created by artist Nate Hallinan in 2014 and may be held back by copyright. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Smurf_Cat]
Los Losers is an upcoming Secret Brainrot in Steal a Brainrot that Sammy leaked on Update 60, but it is not fully confirmed and may be a joke. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Losers]
Los Losers, the unreleased Steal a Brainrot Secret, would show the three owners of the Roblox game 1+ Keyboard Escape. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Losers]
A Speedrun limited time mode is listed as upcoming for Steal a Brainrot, hinted at in a Saturday Admin Abuse. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Upcoming_Content]
A Mining limited time mode is listed as upcoming for Steal a Brainrot, hinted at in Sari's Secret Admin Abuse. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Upcoming_Content]
The Fandom wiki lists an OG Lucky Block and an unknown OG Fuse Brainrot as unreleased Steal a Brainrot content based on hints from Sammy. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/OG]
Rhino Helicopterino and Centrucci Nuclucci are listed as confirmed upcoming Brainrot buffs in Steal a Brainrot. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Upcoming_Content]
Possible upcoming Steal a Brainrot buffs include Brutto Gialutto, Orbi Mochi, Money Money Man, Noo La Polizia, Jackorilla, Quackula, Boba Panda, and Bunnyman. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Upcoming_Content]
Sammy once announced that Steal a Brainrot players will soon be able to move their base to empty base spaces on the map. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Base]
Sammy once said a basement is coming to Steal a Brainrot bases. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Base]
The Fandom wiki lists a possible fourth Steal a Brainrot base floor for Rebirths 20 to 29, which is an estimate and not an announcement. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Base]
Sammy leaked that the Steal a Brainrot Taco Merchant will return with new Brainrots. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Taco_Merchant]
The Steal a Brainrot movie had no release date as of November 2026, and the Fandom wiki's late 2027 to mid-2028 window is a guess. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Steal_a_Brainrot_Movie]
Steal a Brainrot leaks appear in the community server's skibidi-leaks channel, from Sammy in Admin Abuses, or on YouTubers' live streams. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Leaks]
The first Steal a Brainrot leak on the Fandom wiki was La Grande Combinasion in June 2025. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Leaks]

## Scrapped content

Ice Dragon is a scrapped Steal a Brainrot Secret, a Dragon Cannelloni variant for Santa's Fuse that lost a poll to Dragon Gingerini. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Unused_Content]
Disco is a scrapped Steal a Brainrot mutation that Sammy leaked on March 11, 2026, and it might return later. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Disco_Event]
Disco was meant to follow the Divine mutation in Steal a Brainrot, but Sammy replaced it with Cyber after an idea from YouTuber Rustynickle40. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Mutations]
Flappin Clover is a scrapped Secret Brainrot that was meant for the Steal a Brainrot Lucky Pot. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Flappin_Clover]
Rainbow and Gold is a scrapped Steal a Brainrot Brainrot that was meant for the Leprechaun Lucky Block and was replaced by Cloverat Clapat. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Unused_Content]

## Records and milestones

Steal a Brainrot was the first game to pass 25 million concurrent players, in October 2025. [source: https://www.pocketgamer.biz/robloxs-steal-a-brainrot-becomes-first-game-to-surpass-25m-concurrent-players/]
Steal a Brainrot was the second Roblox game to pass 20 million concurrent players, after Grow a Garden. [source: https://www.pocketgamer.biz/robloxs-steal-a-brainrot-becomes-first-game-to-surpass-25m-concurrent-players/]
Steal a Brainrot passed the Grow a Garden concurrent player record of nearly 22.4 million in September 2025. [source: https://www.pocketgamer.biz/robloxs-steal-a-brainrot-becomes-first-game-to-surpass-25m-concurrent-players/]
The Admin War between Steal a Brainrot and Grow a Garden took place in August 2025 and pushed Roblox past 45 million concurrent users by Roblox's own count, a platform record, with trackers reporting about 47 million. [source: https://www.dexerto.com/roblox/roblox-smashes-concurrent-user-record-thanks-to-war-between-two-games-3242035/] [source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1315098/000131509825000326/ex991-q32025shareholderl.htm | id=A16-0029 | type=official | status=confirmed | checked=2026-11-06]
The Extinct Event in September 2025 drove the Steal a Brainrot concurrent player peak that passed Grow a Garden. [source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steal_a_Brainrot]
Steal a Brainrot had 1.1 billion lifetime visits by June 24, 2025, according to Know Your Meme. [source: https://knowyourmeme.com/memes/subcultures/steal-a-brainrot]
Steal a Brainrot held an event to celebrate 10 billion visits with Update 11 in August 2025. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Update_Log/Update_11]
Steal a Brainrot had 30.1 billion lifetime visits when it passed 25 million concurrent players in October 2025. [source: https://www.pocketgamer.biz/robloxs-steal-a-brainrot-becomes-first-game-to-surpass-25m-concurrent-players/]
Steal a Brainrot had more than 55 billion visits by January 2026. [source: https://www.story-kitchen.com/news/story-kitchen-partnering-with-steal-a-brainrot-creators-on-feature-adaptation-of-roblox-game]
Steal a Brainrot had about 74.3 billion visits and about 29.7 million favorites on November 4, 2026. [source: https://games.roblox.com/v1/games?universeIds=7709344486]
Roblox's own Q3 2025 shareholder letter says Steal a Brainrot eclipsed 25 million concurrent players in October 2025. [source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1315098/000131509825000326/ex991-q32025shareholderl.htm | id=A16-0001 | type=official | status=confirmed | confidence=high | pub=2025-10-30 | event=2025-10 | checked=2026-11-06 | note=The letter gives no exact peak figure. PocketGamer.biz reported 25.4 million on October 7, 2025; the exact peak is disputed (see the October conflict record).] [source: https://www.pocketgamer.biz/robloxs-steal-a-brainrot-becomes-first-game-to-surpass-25m-concurrent-players/ | checked=2026-11-06]
Roblox's Q3 2025 shareholder letter says Grow a Garden set a world record of nearly 22 million concurrent players in July 2025, before Steal a Brainrot passed it. [source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1315098/000131509825000326/ex991-q32025shareholderl.htm | id=A16-0002 | type=official | status=confirmed | confidence=high | pub=2025-10-30 | event=2025-07 | checked=2026-11-06 | note=The letter says this was the world record at the time, for most concurrent videogame players.]
Roblox's Q3 2025 shareholder letter says the Roblox platform had over 45 million concurrent users on August 23, 2025. [source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1315098/000131509825000326/ex991-q32025shareholderl.htm | id=A16-0003 | type=official | status=confirmed | confidence=high | pub=2025-10-30 | event=2025-08-23 | checked=2026-11-06 | note=The letter's figure is a floor (over 45 million). Third-party trackers gave 47.3 to 47.4 million for the same day; those are not official.]
Roblox's Q3 2025 shareholder letter says Steal a Brainrot and 99 Nights in the Forest each reached concurrent peaks that would have exceeded Roblox's whole-platform peak of the prior year. [source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1315098/000131509825000326/ex991-q32025shareholderl.htm | id=A16-0004 | type=official | status=confirmed | confidence=high | pub=2025-10-30 | event=2025 | checked=2026-11-06 | note='Last year' is 2024, read from a letter written in 2025. The letter does not give a number for either game.]
Roblox said its Bruno Mars concert inside Steal a Brainrot on January 17, 2026 drew 12.8 million concurrent users. [source: https://www.pocketgamer.biz/roblox-reports-record-128m-concurrent-users-for-bruno-mars-virtual-concert | id=A16-0009 | type=secondary | status=corroborated | confidence=high | pub=2026-01-27 | event=2026-01-17 | checked=2026-11-06 | note=PocketGamer.biz relays Roblox's own announcement. ## Codes and promotions

The Steal a Brainrot codes feature was added on December 13, 2025. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Codes | id=A07-0002 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | event=2025-12-13 | checked=2026-11-06 | note=Community wiki trivia only. No second source checked.]
The first Steal a Brainrot code ever added was for the Festive 67 brainrot and plushie. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Codes | id=A07-0003 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-06 | note=Community wiki trivia only.]
In Steal a Brainrot, codes were moved from the Shop menu to a dedicated Codes button on June 13, 2026. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Codes | id=A07-0004 | type=community | status=corroborated | confidence=medium | event=2026-06-13 | checked=2026-11-06 | note=The wiki gives the exact date. GamesRadar (updated 2026-11-04) says the change happened as of June 2026 and that the Codes button replaced the Shop menu route.] [source: https://www.gamesradar.com/games/simulation/roblox-steal-a-brainrot-codes | checked=2026-11-06]
To redeem a Steal a Brainrot code, click the Codes button on the left side of the screen, type the code into the box and press Submit. ## Trading and economy

SpyderSammy first teased the Trade Machine in Steal a Brainrot through a community poll on January 22, 2026. [source: https://techwiser.com/steal-a-brainrot-trade-machine/ | id=A12-0007 | type=secondary | status=corroborated | confidence=medium | pub=2026-02-22 | event=2026-01-22 | checked=2026-11-06 | note=The Trade Machine wiki page also gives the poll as 1.22.2026 (January 22, 2026). The same article reports over 20,000 votes in favour, which is not recorded here.] [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Trade_Machine | checked=2026-11-06]
Before the Trade Machine, Steal a Brainrot trades often required one player to hand over a Brainrot first, and the taker then locked their base, which often led to scams. [source: https://beebom.com/how-to-trade-in-steal-a-brainrot/ | id=A12-0008 | type=secondary | status=corroborated | confidence=medium | pub=2026-02-22 | checked=2026-11-06 | note=Beebom describes the pre-machine scam pattern. TechWiser says that players trading outside the game were often scammed. Neither is an official statement.] [source: https://techwiser.com/steal-a-brainrot-trade-machine/ | checked=2026-11-06]
The Trade Machine in Steal a Brainrot lets players mark the Brainrots they are looking for, shown as LF. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Trade_Machine | id=A12-0009 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-06 | note=Community wiki trivia. The LF feature date is not given.]
In Steal a Brainrot, a script once let scammers keep the Brainrots that players put into Trade Machine trades, and the wiki says that script was later patched. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Trade_Machine | id=A12-0010 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-06 | note=Community wiki only. No date is given for the script or the patch. The method is not recorded here.]
A scam in Steal a Brainrot had players put mutations on Mythic Lucky Blocks and claim they were Secret or OG Lucky Blocks. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Mythic_Lucky_Block | id=A12-0011 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-06 | note=The wiki says the scam was going around at the time of writing and gives no date. Undated.]
A fake Steal a Brainrot ritual using 2 Lirilì Larilà and 2 Strawberrelli Flamingelli was spread by scammers, and it never spawned a Strawberry Elephant. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Rituals | id=A12-0012 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-06 | note=Community wiki; the scam is undated.]
In Steal a Brainrot, selling a Brainrot from your own base returns half of its original price in cash. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Cash | id=A12-0018 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-06 | note=Community wiki only. Original price is as the wiki uses it; not checked against the game.]
Garama and Madundung is the unofficial currency of Steal a Brainrot trades, and many Brainrot values are based on it, as of November 2026. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Garama_and_Madundung | id=A12-0019 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-06 | note=Community wiki label. The game has no official trading currency, and no official source was found for this label.]
Exist Counts, which show how many of each Brainrot exist in Steal a Brainrot, were added in Update 56. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Exist_Counts | id=A12-0022 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-06 | note=Community wiki. The page does not give the Update 56 date. It says the counts appear in the Index, the Trade Machine, bases and the Trade Plaza book.]
Noobini Pizzanini has the highest exist count of any Brainrot in Steal a Brainrot, according to the community wiki as of November 2026. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Noobini_Pizzanini | id=A12-0023 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-06 | note=The wiki Exist Counts table (https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Exist_Counts, header dated June 2026) lists 439,477,976 for it. Exist counts are leaked or released by the developer and change over time.] [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Exist_Counts | checked=2026-11-06]
SpyderSammy's leaked exist counts for Gorillo Subwoofero in Steal a Brainrot showed 9,585 exists, as of July 7, 2026. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Gorillo_Subwoofero | id=A12-0024 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | event=2026-07-07 | checked=2026-11-06 | note=Community wiki. The same page says it makes it the rarest Mythic in the game by the wiki's own ranking, which is not recorded here.]

## Maps, NPCs and limited time modes

Most Brainrots in Steal a Brainrot come out of the Cave, the map's entrance, and walk down the Red Carpet to be bought. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Red_Carpet | id=A13-0001 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-06]
The Live Spawns panel in Steal a Brainrot stands next to the Red Carpet entrance and shows globally announced OG Brainrot spawns. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Red_Carpet | id=A13-0002 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-06 | note=The Live Spawns Board page says it shows the most recent OG spawns with the spawning player's display name.] [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Live_Spawns_Board | checked=2026-11-06]
The timetables that show Steal a Brainrot's hourly seasonal events stand next to the Robux Shop. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Hourly_Events | id=A13-0003 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-06]
During the Fishing event in Steal a Brainrot, the Fisherman NPC spawned near the Gear Shop, where players could buy Fishing Rods for more luck. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Fishing | id=A13-0005 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-06 | note=The Fishing page says the event is now only run during Admin Abuse.]
The Fishing Event in Steal a Brainrot was revealed on November 14, 2025 at 4:30PM EST. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Fishing_Event | id=A13-0006 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-06 | note=The reveal was on the Community Server and on Roblox. This is a reveal date, not the date the event ran.]
Only three Brainrots have been confirmed from the rare puddles in the Steal a Brainrot Fishing event: Tralaledon, Orcaledon and Capitano Moby. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Fishing | id=A13-0007 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-06]
The Fishing event in Steal a Brainrot is no longer run every hour and is now only run during Admin Abuse, according to the Fandom wiki. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Fishing | id=A13-0008 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-06 | note=As of November 2026. The page says the event formerly occurred every hour.]
Players entered the Escape Tsunami limited time mode in Steal a Brainrot through the LTM Event Machine, then chose a server from its menu. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Escape_Tsunami_LTM | id=A13-0009 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | event=2026-01-24 | checked=2026-11-06]
The Arcadopus NPC in Steal a Brainrot was the gateway to the Escape Tsunami limited time mode, where players could interact with it to access the mode. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Arcadopus | id=A13-0010 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-06 | note=The Escape Tsunami page describes the LTM Event Machine as the entrance, so the two may both apply.]
The Escape Tsunami limited time mode in Steal a Brainrot had a Speed Shop that sold +1, +5 and +10 Speed upgrades for cash or Robux. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Escape_Tsunami_LTM | id=A13-0011 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-06 | note=Cash prices rise with each upgrade bought, while the Robux prices stay the same.]
The Escape Tsunami limited time mode lane in Steal a Brainrot had eight segments, rising from Common Brainrots to High-Tier Secret Brainrots. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Escape_Tsunami_LTM | id=A13-0012 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-06]
A Speed Shop is added each time The Backrooms Event is held in Steal a Brainrot, and players use it to upgrade their speed for the Backrooms. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Backrooms_Event | id=A13-0013 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-06]
The Backrooms Event in Steal a Brainrot offers only Brainrot God New and Secret Brainrots, unlike Escape Tsunami, which covered every rarity below OG. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Backrooms_Event | id=A13-0014 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | event=2026-05-09 | checked=2026-11-06 | note=The page says the Backrooms Event was added on Saturday, May 9th in Update 50.]
Lumaca Malefica, Robo Grafito, Glaciator, Flipa Sandala, Abyssaloco and Rubrikiko are listed as Backrooms Event exclusive Brainrots in Steal a Brainrot. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Backrooms_Event | id=A13-0015 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-06 | note=The page marks each of these as a Backrooms Event Exclusive Brainrot.]
Ballerino Lololo, Skull Skull Skull, Garama and Madundung, and Hydra Dragon Cannelloni were not carried over from Escape Tsunami into the Backrooms Event in Steal a Brainrot. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Backrooms_Event | id=A13-0016 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-06]
Jump for Eggs in Steal a Brainrot has seven islands with five eggs each, and players unlock new islands with XP earned on trampolines near the base.
