### Cash
In Steal a Brainrot, a Brainrot's cash income is its base rate times its multiplier, plus the flat value of each trait, according to the Cash page formula. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Cash | id=C04-0134 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | also=https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Mutations | note=The Cash page gives the formula, but notes that the rates are not exact, and one example does not match.]
In Steal a Brainrot, the Cash page says mutation and trait boosts range from a 1.25x to a 10x multiplier. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Cash | id=C04-0135 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot, the cash multiplier is shown at the entrance of the bases and goes up with each rebirth, with a 2x Cash gamepass, a VIP gamepass and completing the Index as other boosts. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Cash | id=C04-0136 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot, Common is the least valuable Brainrot rarity for cash and OG is the highest paying rarity. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Cash | id=C04-0137 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot, normal mutations can spawn during Hourly Events, while traits can only be obtained during Admin Abuse events run by Sammy or other admins. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Cash | id=C04-0138 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | also=https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Hourly_Events]
In Steal a Brainrot, a Rainbow Ta Ta Ta Ta Sahur with a taco trait is expected from the wiki formula to earn 55 times (10 + 3), but the Cash page says it actually earns 55 times 12. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Cash | id=C04-0139 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Shows the wiki formula does not match the in-game value in this example. See open notes.]
### Stealing
In Steal a Brainrot, Sammy added a 30 second anti-steal cooldown, which made the Moreira Method harder to use. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Methods_Of_Stealing | id=C04-0140 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot, the Spyder Elephant is the only Brainrot that cannot be stolen, because it requires a Spider Chain that costs 6 million Robux. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Stealing | id=C04-0141 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Price may vary by country, per the wiki.]
In Steal a Brainrot, Sammy (SpyderSammy) cannot be stolen from, and trying to steal from him gives an error message. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Stealing | id=C04-0142 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot, Event-Exclusive, Admin Abuse exclusive and Machine exclusive Brainrots can be stolen. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Stealing | id=C04-0143 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot, a Brainrot that you are holding cannot be stolen while you hold it, but you can lose it if you are hit. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Griefing | id=C04-0144 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot, the owner hitting a thief does not count as griefing, because the thief is stealing their Brainrot. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Griefing | id=C04-0145 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot, griefing is when a third player who does not own the base hits the thief after the owner has left, which takes the Brainrot out of the thief's hands and voids it. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Griefing | id=C04-0146 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot, a griefing update made a Brainrot drop on the ground for 2 minutes after the holder was hit, but that update was removed a day later after backlash. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Griefing | id=C04-0147 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot, the Moreira Method, also called the Block Method, is considered scamming and can get the user banned when used against an innocent player. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Methods_Of_Stealing | id=C04-0148 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | note=The wiki lists this as a warning. It is not a recommended method.]
The Steal a Brainrot Methods of Stealing page lists at least 34 numbered stealing methods, each tied to a gear or item. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Methods_Of_Stealing | id=C04-0149 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | also=https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Strategies , https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Advanced_Strategy | note=The wiki says it does not advocate or allow certain methods. Only the count and names are recorded here.]
In Steal a Brainrot, the Trap n' Swap method needs a Body Swap Potion, which requires Rebirth 10. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Methods_Of_Stealing | id=C04-0150 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot, the Grappling Hook method was patched by Sammy (SpyderSammy). [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Methods_Of_Stealing | id=C04-0151 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot, the Ledge Method was patched temporarily on 22 December after an accident, and Sammy (SpyderSammy) then added it back. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Methods_Of_Stealing | id=C04-0152 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot, the Reverse Ledge Method is the only form of the Ledge Method that was not made defunct by Sammy (SpyderSammy) on December 22, due to an accident. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Methods_Of_Stealing | id=C04-0153 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot, the Reverse Grappling Hook method was popularized by YouTuber Steak and is the hardest method on the wiki. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Methods_Of_Stealing | id=C04-0154 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot, the Trap and Swap style methods need traps placed behind a base, and the wiki says a trap holds a player for about 7 seconds. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Advanced_Strategy | id=C04-0155 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | also=https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Strategies]
In Steal a Brainrot, the Medusa's Head is a quick stun that does not need to be aimed, but it has a long cooldown. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Strategies | id=C04-0156 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | also=https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Advanced_Strategy]
In Steal a Brainrot, the Boogie Bomb is recommended over Medusa's Head for defending a base, because it has a wider range and a much shorter cooldown. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Advanced_Strategy | id=C04-0157 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot, the Invisibility Cloak gives a stronger speed boost than the Speed Coil, and it is useful for scouting targets. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Strategies | id=C04-0158 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot, the Body Swapper is recommended to be used while standing on a trap when the base owner is about to lock their base. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Strategies | id=C04-0159 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot, leaving by clicking the X button can take 2 to 5 seconds before you actually leave, so the Roblox leave button is the safer choice. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Advanced_Strategy | id=C04-0160 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot, a player who wants to steal a Brainrot and hit a player should not duel someone who has more rebirths than them, according to the Advanced Strategy page. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Advanced_Strategy | id=C04-0161 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot, Sammy (SpyderSammy) removed the post-duel public server timer that once blocked stealing from you after a return to public servers. ### Strategies
In Steal a Brainrot, you spawn at your base with $100 and a prompt to buy a Common Noobini Pizzanini. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Strategies | id=C04-0303 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot, advanced players usually gain more from stealing Brainrots than from buying them from the conveyor, because good Brainrots rarely spawn. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Strategies | id=C04-0304 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot, the most valuable Brainrots should be stored on the highest floor of a base, since they are harder to steal there. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Strategies | id=C04-0305 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot, Traps are most effective on the third floor, because players cannot jump over or go around them there. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Strategies | id=C04-0306 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot, Sentries can hold off only one player at a time because of their slow fire rate. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Strategies | id=C04-0307 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot, the Quantum Cloner can return a player to a place on the map from anywhere, and it can phase through walls when a clone is spawned while facing a wall. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Strategies | id=C04-0308 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot, the Laser Cape gives a medium range ranged attack and its X-Ray vision can reveal players hiding with an Invisibility Cloak. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Strategies | id=C04-0309 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot, the Gravity Coil lets you jump higher, and the Grappling Hook is the more versatile item. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Strategies | id=C04-0310 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot, the Web Slinger is powerful for helping friends steal, and it is less useful solo because you must hold it for it to work. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Strategies | id=C04-0311 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot, the Bee Stinger auto shoots when pointed and can be paired with the Paintball Gun. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Strategies | id=C04-0312 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot, Beehive and Bee Launcher invert a target's motions and fill their screen with bees, and Boogie Bomb can intensify the effect. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Strategies | id=C04-0313 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot, a Rage Table can hit players from further away, but its long windup makes it hard to use except in tight spaces. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Strategies | id=C04-0314 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot, the Strategies page says mutated Brainrots should be targeted first because they give more income, with Gold at 1.25x, Diamond at 1.5x and Rainbow at 10x. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Strategies | id=C04-0316 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | also=https://www.sportskeeda.com/roblox-news/all-mutations-effects-steal-brainrot]
In Steal a Brainrot, Medusa's Head is recommended against for base defense, because it has a short range and a long cooldown. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Advanced_Strategy | id=C04-0317 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot, traits can be farmed by using flying or movement items such as the Magic Carpet, Witch Broom, Santa Sleigh, Cupid Wings and the Giant Potion so that events fling you less. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Advanced_Strategy | id=C04-0318 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot, rituals are performed by players lining up in a formation while holding specific Brainrots, and they can be done at any time in the game. [source: https://www.sportskeeda.com/roblox-news/steal-brainrot-all-traits-multipliers | id=C04-0319 | type=secondary | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-03 | checked=2026-11-07 | also=https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Traits/Ritual]
In Steal a Brainrot, the Steal and Grab rules for players outside their own base are Steal only, and the Grab/Sell option appears only in your own base. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Grab/Sell | id=C04-0320 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot, Grab was added in the Fuse Machine update, which is Update 10. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Grab/Sell | id=C04-0321 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot, selling a Brainrot is permanent, and the game asks for confirmation only for Mythic, Brainrot God, Secret, Admin, Taco, Spooky, Festive and OG Brainrots. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Grab/Sell | id=C04-0322 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot, grabbing a Brainrot in your base is done by holding E on PC or holding the button on mobile. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Grab/Sell | id=C04-0323 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]

### Lucky Blocks
Steal a Brainrot has 14 Lucky Blocks as of November 2026, including the Mythic, Brainrot God, Secret, Admin, Taco, Los, Spooky, Los Taco Blocks, Festive, Heart, Leprechaun, Egg, Octo and Bee Lucky Blocks. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Lucky_Blocks | id=C11-0095 | type=community | status=corroborated | confidence=high | checked=2026-11-07 | note=The wiki count sentence does not include the Skull Lucky Block (Update 70), which the wiki has its own page for.]
The Steal a Brainrot Lucky Blocks wiki page says people aged 18 or older can open Lucky Blocks in Brazil. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Lucky_Blocks | id=C11-0096 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Wiki note only; not confirmed by Roblox.]
In Steal a Brainrot, Luck does not apply to Lucky Blocks, because a Lucky Block already decides which Brainrot it holds when it first spawns. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Lucky_Blocks | id=C11-0097 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Wiki trivia; important for odds questions.]
Lucky Blocks in Steal a Brainrot formerly had no faces, and the faces were added later, according to the Lucky Blocks wiki page. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Lucky_Blocks | id=C11-0098 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Wiki trivia.]
The Mythic Lucky Block in Steal a Brainrot formerly had a 10-minute timer before it could be opened, and the wiki says it is now READY in all cases. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Mythic_Lucky_Block | id=C11-0099 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Wiki says the timer ended for non-Robux purchases and the Red Carpet.]
The Secret Lucky Block in Steal a Brainrot formerly had a 30-minute timer when bought from the Red Carpet or any method other than Robux. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Secret_Lucky_Block | id=C11-0100 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
The Brainrot God Lucky Block in Steal a Brainrot formerly had a 15-minute timer before it could be opened. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Brainrot_God_Lucky_Block | id=C11-0101 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
The Mythic Lucky Block, Brainrot God Lucky Block and Secret Lucky Block were the only three Lucky Blocks with a timer in Steal a Brainrot, according to the Lucky Blocks wiki page. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Lucky_Blocks | id=C11-0102 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Update 62 removed the timers; that is already a sheet fact.]
If you put the Mythic Lucky Block in any Fuse Machine in Steal a Brainrot, its icon will not appear and its timer will be stopped. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Mythic_Lucky_Block | id=C11-0103 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
The Mythic Lucky Block in Steal a Brainrot has no glow around it in the menu, which is how to tell it apart from a Secret Lucky Block when trading, according to the wiki. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Mythic_Lucky_Block | id=C11-0104 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
A scam in Steal a Brainrot puts mutations on the Mythic Lucky Block and claims it is a Secret or OG Lucky Block, according to the Mythic Lucky Block wiki page. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Mythic_Lucky_Block | id=C11-0105 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Wiki trivia; date not given.]
The Mythic Lucky Block in Steal a Brainrot has the most generous odds of any Lucky Block, because its rarest Brainrot, Bananito Bandito, is at a 3% chance. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Mythic_Lucky_Block | id=C11-0106 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Wiki trivia opinion phrased as fact on the wiki.]
The Mythic Lucky Block in Steal a Brainrot started with three Brainrots, Spioniro Golubiro, Zibra Zubra Zibralini and Tigrilini Watermelini, and Carrotini Brainini and Bananito Bandito were added later. ### Rituals
The Bombardiro Crocodilo ritual in Steal a Brainrot needs three players holding a Bombardiro Crocodilo in a line at the Red Carpet, and it spawns the Brainrot God Los Crocodillitos generating $55K/s. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Rituals | id=C11-0158 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
The Bombardiro Crocodilo ritual in Steal a Brainrot starts the Bombardiro Bombing weather, and the wiki calls it the cheapest ritual to perform. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Rituals | id=C11-0159 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
The Bombardiro Crocodilo ritual in Steal a Brainrot has an income-after value of +$47.5K/s. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Rituals | id=C11-0160 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Income After column of the Rituals table.]
The Orcalero Orcala ritual in Steal a Brainrot needs four players to steal or grab an Orcalero Orcala or Orcalita Orcala, and it spawns the Brainrot God Los Orcalitos generating $235K/s with the Ocean weather. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Rituals | id=C11-0161 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
The Orcalero Orcala ritual in Steal a Brainrot was added in Update 11. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Update_Log/Update_11 | id=C11-0162 | type=community | status=corroborated | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Update 11 date is not confirmed from this page; the sheet has August 2025 for Update 11 from another record.]
The Orcalero Orcala ritual in Steal a Brainrot is generally considered useless, because Los Orcalitos can be obtained from the Los Lucky Blocks, and most players do it for the Shark Fin trait. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Rituals | id=C11-0163 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Wiki trivia opinion.]
The Matteo ritual in Steal a Brainrot was reworked in Update 12 so that it gives a trait and Los Matteos. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Update_Log/Update_12 | id=C11-0164 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Update 12 release date is not stated on this page.]
The Matteo ritual in Steal a Brainrot needs three players stacked on top of each other holding a Matteo, and it spawns the Secret Los Matteos generating $325K/s, with a tree sprouting and the Matteo's Hat weather starting. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Rituals | id=C11-0165 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Sportskeeda and an older guide say four players; see the open file.]
The Matteo ritual in Steal a Brainrot has an income-after value of +$175K/s. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Rituals | id=C11-0166 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
The La Vacca Saturno Saturnita ritual in Steal a Brainrot needs three players holding a La Vacca Saturno Saturnita in a triangle, starts the Meteor Shower weather, and spawns the Secret Las Vaquitas Saturnitas generating $750K/s. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Rituals | id=C11-0167 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
The La Vacca Saturno Saturnita ritual in Steal a Brainrot has an income-after value of -$225K/s. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Rituals | id=C11-0168 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Income After column; the sign and value are from the table.]
The Sammyni Spyderini ritual in Steal a Brainrot starts the Sammyni Spyderini Invasion weather, which includes a giant cobweb on the map. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Rituals | id=C11-0169 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
The Chicleteira Bicicleteira ritual in Steal a Brainrot triggers the Chicleteira Bicicleteira event, which makes a road come out of the ground and spawns the Secret Los Chicleteiras generating $7M/s. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Rituals | id=C11-0170 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
The Dul Dul Dul ritual in Steal a Brainrot needs four Dul Dul Dul in a square away from the Red Carpet, and it spawns Yess my Examen at 95% or Noo my Examen at 5%, along with the Graduation Tie formation. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Rituals | id=C11-0171 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
Noo my Examen from the Dul Dul Dul ritual in Steal a Brainrot generates $32.5M/s, and Yess my Examen generates $575K/s. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Rituals | id=C11-0172 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
The Karkerkar Kurkur ritual in Steal a Brainrot needs four Karkerkar Kurkur placed in a cube, then a musical chairs game starts, and the Secret Los Karkeritos spawns generating $750K/s. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Rituals | id=C11-0174 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Conflicts with the sheet line describing a diamond shape; see the open file.]
The Karkerkar Kurkur ritual in Steal a Brainrot is the first ritual that does not spawn an event or mutation. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Rituals | id=C11-0175 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
The Guerriro Digitale ritual in Steal a Brainrot works at 3 AM EST, or during Admin Abuse, when Sammy spawns the Guerriro Digitale for it, and it can give 1x1x1x1, John Doe or Guest 666. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Rituals | id=C11-0176 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
According to Sammy, the Guerriro Digitale ritual in Steal a Brainrot gives 1x1x1x1 at 94%, John Doe at 5% and Guest 666 at 1%, with Guest 666 formerly at 0.5%. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/1x1x1x1_Ritual_Event | id=C11-0177 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Conflicts with the older sheet line giving 99.5% and 0.5%; see the open file.]
The Guerriro Digitale ritual in Steal a Brainrot has income-after values of -$1.1M/s for 1x1x1x1, +$5.3M/s for John Doe and +$64.46M/s for Guest 666. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Rituals | id=C11-0178 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | note=The wiki table lists these values in one cell; the John Doe and Guest 666 figures are in the same table row.]
The Mi Gatito ritual in Steal a Brainrot needs two Mi Gatito facing each other so they hug, which plays the :3 event and spawns the Los Mi Gatitos generating $6.5M/s. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Rituals | id=C11-0179 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
The soundtrack of the Los Mi Gatitos event in Steal a Brainrot is MONTAGEM MIAU, made by Lenar. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Soundtracks/Rituals | id=C11-0180 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
The Job Job Job Sahur ritual in Steal a Brainrot triggers the Job Application weather and spawns Yess my Resume at 99% or Noo my Resume at 1%, with Yess my Resume generating $2.1M/s and Noo my Resume generating $32.5M/s. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Rituals | id=C11-0181 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
The Money Money Puggy ritual in Steal a Brainrot starts the Money Rain event, which spawns Los Puggies, and the ritual needs two Money Money Puggy in front of the Robux Shop. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Rituals | id=C11-0182 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Quote is from the wiki table cell.]
The Money Money Puggy ritual in Steal a Brainrot is the best ritual that is not randomized, according to the Fandom wiki. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Rituals | id=C11-0183 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
The Guest 666 ritual result is the best ritual Brainrot in Steal a Brainrot, according to the wiki, and it is worth $59.6M/s more than Los Chicleteiras. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Rituals | id=C11-0184 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Wiki says Guest 666 was buffed; the figure comes from the trivia.]
The RNG Machine in Steal a Brainrot contains nine ritual Brainrots, and the wiki says this made rituals easier to do. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Rituals | id=C11-0185 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
The Rituals page lists ten rituals in Steal a Brainrot as of November 2026, including the Bombardiro, La Vacca, Orcalero, Matteo, Spyderini, Chicleteira Bicicleteira, Dul Dul Dul, Karkerkar Kurkur and Guerriro Digitale rituals. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Rituals | id=C11-0186 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Some older guides list seven rituals.]
The Los Orcalitos ritual in Steal a Brainrot uses the Underwater soundtrack, which is also used when Sammy activates the underwater event. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Soundtracks/Rituals | id=C11-0187 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
The Las Vaquitas Saturnitas ritual in Steal a Brainrot uses the Space soundtrack, which is also heard during some Admin Abuses. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Soundtracks/Rituals | id=C11-0188 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
The Los Matteos ritual in Steal a Brainrot uses the Matteo's Nature soundtrack, and the Spider Invasion soundtrack plays for the Los Spyderinis ritual. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Soundtracks/Rituals | id=C11-0189 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Combined from two rows of the soundtrack table.]
Los Karkeritos from the Karkerkar Kurkur ritual in Steal a Brainrot is said to head to the winner of the musical chairs game base. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Rituals | id=C11-0190 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
Fake Steal a Brainrot rituals on video sites claim to raise the chance of Strawberry Elephant, but the ritual has never spawned Strawberry Elephant according to the wiki. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Rituals | id=C11-0191 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | note=The wiki says the video creators were scammers.]
Super Thin Tall, a common avatar bundle, can stop Steal a Brainrot rituals from lining up correctly for other players, according to the Fandom wiki. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Rituals | id=C11-0192 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
The Steal a Brainrot Chicleteira Bicicleteira, Mi Gatito and Money Money Puggy rituals each need only two specific Brainrots, which is the fewest of any ritual. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Rituals | id=C11-0193 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
The Orcalero Orcala ritual in Steal a Brainrot needs four Orcalero Orcala or Orcalita Orcala, and the wiki says some people did not know Orcalita Orcala works. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Rituals | id=C11-0194 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
The Guerriro Digitale ritual in Steal a Brainrot is called the 1x1x1x1 ritual by fans, because 1x1x1x1 is better known than Guerriro Digitale. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Rituals | id=C11-0195 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
The 1x1x1x1 Ritual Event in Steal a Brainrot opens the 1x1x1x1 cave every morning at 3:00 AM EST and 4:00 AM EDT for five minutes, and it is the only ritual that is only doable at a set time. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/1x1x1x1_Ritual_Event | id=C11-0196 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
The 1x1x1x1 Ritual Event in Steal a Brainrot is not time-shifted for Eastern Daylight Time, so during EDT it runs at 4:00 AM instead of 3:00 AM. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/1x1x1x1_Ritual_Event | id=C11-0197 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
The 1x1x1x1 Ritual Event in Steal a Brainrot ran permanently from May 23, 2026 to June 13, 2026 during Update 52, and players could view Sammy working on his computer during that time. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/1x1x1x1_Ritual_Event | id=C11-0198 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Wiki spells the date as May 23th.]
The 1x1x1x1 Ritual Event in Steal a Brainrot was run for three hours on March 18, 2026 for the John Doe hacking. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/1x1x1x1_Ritual_Event | id=C11-0199 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Wiki wording is 1x1x1x1 Ritual Event was spawned for 3 hours.]
The Glitch Event in Steal a Brainrot runs during the 1x1x1x1 Ritual Event and gives brainrots a chance to fall in a hole while walking and gain the Glitched trait. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/1x1x1x1_Ritual_Event | id=C11-0200 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
### Red Carpet spawn rates
The Red Carpet in Steal a Brainrot uses RoadWeight values to decide spawns, and the wiki says these values are not percentages or X out of X chances. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Red_Carpet | id=C11-0201 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Wiki says the values were extracted from game files as RoadWeight.]
In Steal a Brainrot, the Red Carpet RoadWeight values for Brainrot Gods, Secrets and OG Brainrots were stored in the ServerStorage folder from September 6, 2025, so the latest OG values are estimates. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Red_Carpet | id=C11-0202 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | event=2025-09-06 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Wiki says estimated OG values are marked as estimates.]
In Steal a Brainrot, a Legendary Brainrot is guaranteed to appear on the Red Carpet after about five minutes, and a Mythic Brainrot after about 15 minutes, according to the wiki. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Red_Carpet | id=C11-0203 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Wiki guarantee times; the Brainrot God time is estimated, see the next fact.]
In Steal a Brainrot, a Brainrot God is guaranteed to appear on the Red Carpet after about 45 minutes, which the wiki says is an estimate. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Red_Carpet | id=C11-0204 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Estimated by the wiki, not from game files.]
The Gold mutation has a RoadWeight of 7, the Diamond mutation has 3 and the Rainbow mutation has 0.2 on the Red Carpet in Steal a Brainrot, according to the wiki. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Red_Carpet | id=C11-0205 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
During Christmas, Gold Elf in Steal a Brainrot had no RoadWeight and instead had a 1 in 500 (0.2%) chance to spawn on the Red Carpet for every Brainrot that spawned. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Red_Carpet | id=C11-0206 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
Cooki and Milki in Steal a Brainrot used to be obtainable on the Red Carpet before they were put into Santa's Fuse. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Red_Carpet | id=C11-0207 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
Noobini Pizzanini has the highest Red Carpet RoadWeight of any Brainrot in Steal a Brainrot, at 100, which the wiki uses as the reference point. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Red_Carpet | id=C11-0208 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Derived from the wiki table: 100 is the top value listed.]
Noobini Pizzanini has a Red Carpet RoadWeight of 100 in Steal a Brainrot, and its rarity is Common. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Red_Carpet | id=C11-0209 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | note=RoadWeight is a weight, not a percentage, per the wiki. ### Luck variants
The 2x Luck variant in Steal a Brainrot is listed at R$249 on the Luck wiki page, and it can come from Admin Abuse, Wheel Spins and the Advent Calendar. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Luck | id=C11-0320 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | also=https://techwiser.com/all-items-in-steal-a-brainrot-roblox/ | note=TechWiser lists the 2x server luck at 249 Robux, 15 minutes, updated December 26, 2025.]
The 4x Luck variant in Steal a Brainrot is listed at R$499 on the Luck wiki page, and it can come from Admin Abuse and the Advent Calendar. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Luck | id=C11-0321 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Conflicts with the Sportskeeda and TechWiser 999 Robux figure; see the existing Needs review conflict for Server Luck 4x.]
The 8x Luck variant in Steal a Brainrot is a Rainbow luck variant listed at R$2999, and the wiki says Sammy made it purchasable on February 7, 2026. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Luck | id=C11-0322 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | event=2026-02-07 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Wiki trivia also says only 2x Luck can be bought now, which conflicts with this; see the open file.]
The 6x Luck variant in Steal a Brainrot comes from Admin Abuse and Admin Machines, according to the Luck wiki page. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Luck | id=C11-0323 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
The 10x Luck variant in Steal a Brainrot is a Secret-rarity luck variant that comes from Admin Abuse and Admin Machines. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Luck | id=C11-0324 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
The 12x Luck variant in Steal a Brainrot is an OG-rarity luck variant, and the wiki says it may only give good Brainrot Gods and normal Secrets. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Luck | id=C11-0325 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
The 15x Luck variant in Steal a Brainrot is a Festive luck variant that appeared in Admin Abuse during Christmas 2025. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Luck | id=C11-0326 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
The 20x Luck variant in Steal a Brainrot is a Candy-mutation-styled luck variant that appeared in Admin Abuse during Valentines 2026. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Luck | id=C11-0327 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
The 25x Luck variant in Steal a Brainrot is a Radioactive-styled luck variant that appeared in Admin Abuse during Saint Patrick's Day 2026. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Luck | id=C11-0328 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
The 30x Luck variant in Steal a Brainrot appeared in Admin Abuse during the 1 Year Celebration in 2026, and the wiki says Sammy spawns it very rarely. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Luck | id=C11-0329 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | event=2026-05-16 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Update 51 date from the sheet.]
The 35x Luck variant in Steal a Brainrot appeared in Admin Abuse during Summer 2026, and the wiki says Sammy spawns it very rarely. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Luck | id=C11-0330 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
The 15x, 20x and 25x Luck variants in Steal a Brainrot are the only luck multipliers limited to a holiday, according to the Luck wiki page. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Luck | id=C11-0331 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
Before the Valentine's update in Steal a Brainrot, Luck had only two purchasable variants, 2x and 4x, and 8x was made purchasable later. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Luck | id=C11-0333 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
Sammy (SpyderSammy) once said he would activate 100x Luck for one minute in Steal a Brainrot, according to the Luck wiki page. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Luck | id=C11-0334 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Wiki trivia, a stated intention, not a confirmed event.]
Sammy (SpyderSammy) can set Luck in Steal a Brainrot to any value, according to the Luck wiki page. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Luck | id=C11-0335 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot, the mini admin abuse in which Sammy activated x10 Luck and a snap took place at 11:50 PM EST, according to the Admin Abuse wiki page. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Admin_Abuse | id=C11-0336 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Admin Abuse wiki says 23h50 EST, which is 11:50 PM EST.]
### Spawn sounds and explosions
The Spooky Explosion in Steal a Brainrot is an orange, spooky explosion that plays whenever a Spooky Lucky Block spawns. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Sound_Effects/Spawns | id=C11-0338 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
The Christmas Explosion in Steal a Brainrot is a green and red explosion that plays whenever a Festive Lucky Block spawns. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Sound_Effects/Spawns | id=C11-0339 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
The Valentines Explosion in Steal a Brainrot is a pink explosion that plays whenever a Valentines Brainrot or the Heart Lucky Block spawns. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Sound_Effects/Spawns | id=C11-0340 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
The St. Patrick's Explosion in Steal a Brainrot is a green and yellow explosion with coins that plays whenever a St. Patrick's Brainrot or the Leprechaun Lucky Block spawns. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Sound_Effects/Spawns | id=C11-0341 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
The Easter Explosion in Steal a Brainrot is a cyan and pink explosion that plays whenever an Easter Brainrot or the Egg Lucky Block spawns, and the Summer Explosion is a blue explosion for Summer Brainrots and the Octo Lucky Block. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Sound_Effects/Spawns | id=C11-0342 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Combined from the Easter/Summer row of the wiki table.]
The Taco Explosion in Steal a Brainrot is a super-charged taco explosion that plays whenever a Taco Brainrot, Taco Truck Brainrot, the Taco Lucky Block or the Los Taco Blocks spawn. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Sound_Effects/Spawns | id=C11-0343 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
The 1x1x1x1 Explosion in Steal a Brainrot plays at the 1x1x1x1 cave whenever 1x1x1x1 spawns, and the Guest 666 and John Doe Explosion plays there for those two Brainrots. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Sound_Effects/Spawns | id=C11-0344 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Combined from two rows of the wiki table.]
The Spray Paint Explosion in Steal a Brainrot is a multi-colored explosion that plays whenever Los Chicleteiras spawn. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Sound_Effects/Spawns | id=C11-0345 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
The Spyder Explosion in Steal a Brainrot is a white explosion with a spider symbol that plays whenever Los Spyderinis spawn. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Sound_Effects/Spawns | id=C11-0346 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
The Leafs Explosion for Los Matteos in Steal a Brainrot is a green explosion, and unlike Matteo's spawn, it does not play the voice saying Matteo. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Sound_Effects/Spawns | id=C11-0347 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
The Cat Explosion in Steal a Brainrot is a pink and cyan explosion that plays whenever Mi Gatito or Los Mi Gatitos spawn. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Sound_Effects/Spawns | id=C11-0348 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Evidence line may vary; checked later.]
In Steal a Brainrot, Craft Machine lasers are colored by rarity: purple for Epic, yellow for Legendary, red for Mythic, rainbow for Brainrot God, and white and black for Secret. ### Live Spawns Board
The Live Spawns Board in Steal a Brainrot only shows OG Brainrot spawns, so that the board does not crash from too many updates. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Live_Spawns_Board | id=C11-0355 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Wiki says the restriction is to avoid crashing the board.]
In Steal a Brainrot, if a player does not claim an OG spawn shown on the Live Spawns Board within three minutes, the wiki says they are probably trait farming it. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Live_Spawns_Board | id=C11-0356 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
The Live Spawns Board in Steal a Brainrot shows many OG Brainrots at high luck, such as 10x Secret, 12x OG, 15x Festive, 20x Candy and 25x Radioactive Luck, according to the wiki. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Live_Spawns_Board | id=C11-0357 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
### Fishing and Lucky Catch
The Fishing mechanic in Steal a Brainrot was removed from the game and is now only available as an Admin Abuse event. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Fishing | id=C11-0358 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Wiki says it is now only Admin Abuse Exclusive.]
In Steal a Brainrot, the Fisherman NPC appears near the Gear Shop during the Fishing event, and players can buy Fishing Rods there for more luck. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Fishing | id=C11-0359 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot, only Tralaledon, Orcaledon and Capitano Moby have been confirmed to come from the Fishing rare puddles, according to the Fishing wiki page. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Fishing | id=C11-0360 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot, the first person to fish a rare puddle gets the Brainrot inside it, according to the Fishing wiki page. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Fishing | id=C11-0361 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot, catching a fish requires casting a rod on the ground level during the Fishing event and clicking enough times when a Brainrot bites. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Fishing | id=C11-0362 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
There are no Mythic Brainrots in the Steal a Brainrot Fishing event, according to the wiki. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Fishing | id=C11-0363 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
The Steal a Brainrot fishing list has Trippi Troppi as its only Rare Brainrot, Trulimero Trulicina and Bananita Dolphinita as Epic, and Blueberrinni Octopusini and Puffaball as Legendary. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Fishing | id=C11-0364 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Evidence line is the first fishable Rare entry on the wiki page.]
In Steal a Brainrot, Fishino Clownino is unobtainable from fishing because its exist count is low and Sammy wants it to stay rare, according to the Fishing wiki page. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Fishing | id=C11-0365 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot, the water during Fishing event Candy, Galaxy, Bloodrot and Yin Yang mutation events turns pink, purple, dark red and white, and each event allows fishing for that mutation. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Fishing | id=C11-0366 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Combined from the wiki page; these mutation events are currently admin-only.]
The Fishing Event in Steal a Brainrot has Radioactive and Aquatic indexes, and each index gives a base reward after a player collects 90 percent of its Brainrots, according to the Fishing Event wiki page. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Fishing_Event | id=C11-0367 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
### Egg spawning and Egg Incubator
The Egg Incubator machine in Steal a Brainrot is listed by the wiki with 12 Brainrots, and 13 counting the Egg Lucky Block. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Egg_Incubator | id=C11-0368 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Wiki infobox value for the machine.]
In Steal a Brainrot, if you put an egg into the Egg Incubator and then duel, the egg is gone afterward, which was listed as a bug on the wiki. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Egg_Incubator | id=C11-0370 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
The Egg Incubator wiki page in Steal a Brainrot lists these eggs: Bunny Tralala, Eggdin Egg Egg Dun, Egg Lucky Block, Buntteo, Easter Easter Easter Sahur, Bunny Bunny Bunny Sahur, Noo my Eggs, Los Bunitos, Baskito, Churrito Bunnito, Quackini Snackini, Hopilikalika Hopilikalako and Hydra Bunny. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Egg_Incubator | id=C11-0371 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Egg list from the wiki Eggs section; the page does not say the list is complete.]
### Admin Abuse spawns
In Steal a Brainrot Admin Abuse, Sammy always spawns the Mythic, Brainrot God, Taco, Los Taco Blocks, Admin, Los Lucky Blocks and Secret Lucky Blocks, according to the wiki. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Admin_Abuse | id=C11-0372 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Los Taco Blocks are the most commonly spawned in the highest quantity.]
In Steal a Brainrot Admin Abuse, the Lucky Blocks that Sammy does not always spawn are the Spooky, Festive, Heart, Leprechaun and Egg Lucky Blocks, and the wiki says some may never return. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Admin_Abuse | id=C11-0373 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot Admin Abuse, Sammy most often spawns Matteo, La Vacca Saturno Saturnita, Karkerkar Kurkur, Dul Dul Dul, Los Tralaleritos, Las Tralaleritas, Job Job Job Sahur, Graipuss Medussi, To to to Sahur and Chicleteira Bicicleteira, according to the wiki. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Admin_Abuse | id=C11-0374 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot Admin Abuse, Sammy's base always has at least three Brainrots and can have up to six, with the most common ones being Ballerino Lololo and Tartaruga Cisterna. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Admin_Abuse | id=C11-0375 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Evidence line is the wiki text; the Ballerino and Tartaruga detail is also on the same page.]
In Steal a Brainrot, Sammy holds Secret Admin Abuses, which the wiki says happen mostly on Sundays and Friday nights and can be a snap or a 30-minute event. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Admin_Abuse | id=C11-0376 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot, Sammy spawns La Vacca Saturno Saturnita most often in public servers during weekend Admin Abuses, according to the wiki. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Admin_Abuse | id=C11-0377 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot, Sammy increases Server Luck and spawns weather and events during an Admin Abuse, which can give special traits. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Red_Carpet | id=C11-0378 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot, Admin Abuses also happen in private servers, which the wiki says can reduce competition for Brainrots. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Admin_Abuse | id=C11-0379 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]

## Items, gear, places and NPCs

### Slaps and melee gears
The Diamond Slap in Steal a Brainrot costs 50,000 Cash, needs 3 rebirths, and is a stronger version of the Gold Slap. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Gears | id=C05-0001 | type=community | status=corroborated | confidence=high | checked=2026-11-07 | also=https://techwiser.com/all-items-in-steal-a-brainrot-roblox/ , https://www.sportskeeda.com/roblox-news/all-steal-brainrot-weapons | note=Sportskeeda lists 50,000 Cash and 3 rebirths. The Fandom page notes the Diamond Slap cannot actually be charged up.]
The Emerald Slap in Steal a Brainrot costs 200,000 Cash, needs 4 rebirths, and is a stronger version of the Diamond Slap. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Slap | id=C05-0002 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | also=https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Gears]
The Ruby Slap in Steal a Brainrot costs 1 million Cash and needs 5 rebirths, and is a stronger version of the Emerald Slap. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Slap | id=C05-0003 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | also=https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Gears]
The Dark Matter Slap in Steal a Brainrot costs 1.5 million Cash and needs 6 rebirths, and is a stronger version of the Ruby Slap. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Slap | id=C05-0004 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | also=https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Gears]
The Flame Slap in Steal a Brainrot costs 2.5 million Cash and needs 7 rebirths, and is a stronger version of the Dark Matter Slap. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Slap | id=C05-0005 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | also=https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Gears]
The Nuclear Slap in Steal a Brainrot costs 6 million Cash and needs 8 rebirths, and is a stronger version of the Flame Slap. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Slap | id=C05-0006 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | also=https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Gears]
The Rainbowrath Sword in Steal a Brainrot costs 10 million Cash and needs 8 rebirths, and lunges forward and flings any player in the way on every third swing. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Gears | id=C05-0010 | type=community | status=corroborated | confidence=high | checked=2026-11-07 | also=https://www.sportskeeda.com/roblox-news/all-steal-brainrot-weapons | note=Sportskeeda lists 10,000,000 Cash and 8 rebirths. The Fandom page says it can sometimes glitch and kill the player hit.]
### Coin shop gears
The Rage Table in Steal a Brainrot costs 25,000 Cash and needs 2 rebirths, and it is thrown to fling players and return your Brainrots. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Gears | id=C05-0013 | type=community | status=corroborated | confidence=high | checked=2026-11-07 | also=https://www.sportskeeda.com/roblox-news/all-steal-brainrot-weapons , https://techwiser.com/all-items-in-steal-a-brainrot-roblox/ | note=Sportskeeda lists 25,000 Cash. The Fandom page gives a 4 second cooldown. TechWiser's summarized table gives 2 rebirths.]
The Subspace Mine in Steal a Brainrot costs 500 million Cash, needs 14 rebirths, and lets a player hold up to 2 placed mines at once. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Gears | id=C05-0014 | type=community | status=corroborated | confidence=high | checked=2026-11-07 | also=https://techwiser.com/all-items-in-steal-a-brainrot-roblox/ | note=The mine explodes when another player touches it while it is fully invisible. Cooldown is 15 seconds for the first mine and 20 seconds for the second.]
The Body Swap Potion in Steal a Brainrot costs 50 million Cash, needs 10 rebirths, and swaps your position with the affected player. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Gears | id=C05-0017 | type=community | status=corroborated | confidence=high | checked=2026-11-07 | also=https://techwiser.com/all-items-in-steal-a-brainrot-roblox/ | note=Cooldown is 30 seconds on the Fandom page.]
The All-Seeing Sentry in Steal a Brainrot costs 5 million Cash and needs 7 rebirths. It shoots other players in range, even through walls, after 5 seconds of preparation. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Gears | id=C05-0018 | type=community | status=corroborated | confidence=high | checked=2026-11-07 | also=https://www.sportskeeda.com/roblox-news/all-steal-brainrot-weapons , https://techwiser.com/all-items-in-steal-a-brainrot-roblox/ | note=The sentry lasts up to 1 minute and can be destroyed with Slap tools.]
The Flash Teleport in Steal a Brainrot costs 3 billion Cash, needs 18 rebirths, and teleports the player a short distance to a marked spot. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Gears | id=C05-0019 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | also=https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Gears | note=The Fandom page says the ghost marker lets you teleport to higher ground when you zoom the camera up. Cooldown is 20 seconds.]
The Quantum Cloner in Steal a Brainrot was originally named Quantum Entangler, based on an official Roblox gear. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Gears | id=C05-0022 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Fandom says most Steal a Brainrot gears are based on official Roblox gears, and some had names or functions changed.]
The gear shop in Steal a Brainrot has 40 obtainable gears, according to the Fandom wiki. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Gears | id=C05-0023 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Fandom's count as of the page's last edit, not a live count.]
The Bloodmoon Slap and the Bloodmoon Hammer in Steal a Brainrot were the first Wheel items, since the Bloodrot Wheel was the first wheel to offer gears. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Gears | id=C05-0024 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | also=https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Wheels]

### Interactables and NPCs
The Pole Game in Steal a Brainrot is a Panjat Pinang mini event released on October 18, 2025 at 9:00 AM EST, and it is part of the Indonesian Event. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Pole_Game | id=C05-0094 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2025-10-18 | event=2025-10-18 | checked=2026-11-07]

[source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Pole_Game | id=C05-0095 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
The Piñata in Steal a Brainrot is an event object from the México Event that releases only candy or a Brainrot when destroyed. ### Admin Abuse
Admin Abuse in Steal a Brainrot is run every Saturday after the weekly update, usually at 3PM EST, and typically lasts 30 to 60 minutes. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Admin_Abuse | id=C06-0036 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
Sammy gives an early bird present, usually a Secret Lucky Block, to Steal a Brainrot players who are online about one hour before an Admin Abuse begins. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Admin_Abuse | id=C06-0037 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=high | checked=2026-11-07]
### Admin Abuse guaranteed lucky blocks
Sammy always spawns the Mythic, Brainrot God, Taco, Los Taco Blocks, Admin, Los and Secret Lucky Blocks during an Admin Abuse in Steal a Brainrot, with Los Taco Blocks being the most common. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Admin_Abuse | id=C06-0038 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=high | checked=2026-11-07]
The Spooky, Festive, Heart, Leprechaun and Egg Lucky Blocks are not guaranteed to be spawned by Sammy during Admin Abuse in Steal a Brainrot, and the wiki says each may never return after its holiday update. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Admin_Abuse | id=C06-0039 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
Sammy's Snap in Steal a Brainrot is an animation where Sammy runs from the start of the Red Carpet and grows until he snaps, starting almost all in-game events at once. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Admin_Abuse | id=C06-0040 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=high | checked=2026-11-07]
The Coffin Snap in Steal a Brainrot is a Sammy's Snap variant where Sammy comes out of a coffin before the snap. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Admin_Abuse | id=C06-0041 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=high | checked=2026-11-07]
Sammy's Random Server Spawns in Steal a Brainrot pick a set number of servers and spawn a chosen brainrot in each one, showing players a message that Sammy has spawned it in their server. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Admin_Abuse | id=C06-0042 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=high | checked=2026-11-07]
The Admin Abuse secret admin abuses in Steal a Brainrot are run mostly on Sundays and Friday nights, and often last 30 minutes or less. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Admin_Abuse | id=C06-0043 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Duration wording taken from the same section ('whole 30 minute long events').]
The Admin Abuse Exclusive events in Steal a Brainrot include Raining Tacos, UFO, Crab Rave, Tung Tung Attack, Solar Flare, Nyan Cat, Rap concert, Bubblegum, Brazil, Indonesian, Mexico, Piñata and Panjat Pinang. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Events | id=C06-0046 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=high | checked=2026-11-07 | note=List from the Admin Abuse Exclusive Events table on the Events page.]
The UFO event in Steal a Brainrot is an Admin Abuse exclusive where a UFO abducts random brainrots and gives them the UFO trait. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Events | id=C06-0047 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=high | checked=2026-11-07]

### Admin Abuse War
The Admin Abuse War in Steal a Brainrot was declared by Jandel, the owner of Grow a Garden, who said Sammy copied the concept of Admin Abuses. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Admin_Abuse_War | id=C06-0085 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=high | event=2025-08-23 | checked=2026-11-07]
During the Admin Abuse War in Steal a Brainrot, Sammy spawned the Galaxy Introduction rocket, which took players into the Galaxy event, and the Galaxy Introduction ran twice in the war. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Admin_Abuse_War | id=C06-0086 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | event=2025-08-23 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Galaxy Introduction twice-run line is from the Removed Events table on the Events page.]
The Sleepy event in Steal a Brainrot was run once for the Admin Abuse War and gave brainrots the Sleepy trait, and it was never played again. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Events | id=C06-0087 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=high | event=2025-08-23 | checked=2026-11-07]
In the Admin Abuse War in Steal a Brainrot, Sammy activated 6x luck and then 8x luck during the crab rave portion. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Admin_Abuse_War | id=C06-0088 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | event=2025-08-23 | checked=2026-11-07]
Roblox reached about 47.4 million concurrent players during the Admin Abuse War week in August 2025, with Steal a Brainrot and Grow a Garden accounting for most of them. ### John Doe, Granny, Like Goal and community
The John Doe Hacking event in Steal a Brainrot happened on March 18, 2026, starting around 3:00 to 3:30 PM EST, when a hacker using the John Doe name took control of the game and posted taunts like W JANDEL. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/John_Doe_Hacking | id=C06-0162 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=high | event=2026-03-18 | checked=2026-11-07]
The John Doe hacking in Steal a Brainrot ended with the 1x1x1x1 Event being activated by the hacker. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/John_Doe_Hacking | id=C06-0163 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | event=2026-03-18 | checked=2026-11-07]
John Doe, the alias used in the March 18, 2026 hack of Steal a Brainrot, is an old Roblox test account created by David Baszucki and Erik Cassel on June 25, 2005. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/John_Doe_Hacking | id=C06-0164 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | event=2026-03-18 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=The 2017 rumor line and the test account line are both on the page's trivia; evidence is the rumor line.]
A real hacking of Steal a Brainrot happened on October 22, 2026, when a hacked developer spawned Rainbow Headless Horsemans in all servers, and the game was shut down for an hour. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/John_Doe_Hacking | id=C06-0165 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | event=2026-10-22 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Page says the game was shut down for an hour while Sammy deleted the Headlesses.]
Sammy posted RIP our granny she got hit by a bazooka on Saturday March 21, 2026 about two hours before Granny's Funeral started in an Admin Abuse in Steal a Brainrot. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Granny's_Funeral | id=C06-0166 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=high | event=2026-03-21 | checked=2026-11-07]
The Like Goal Milestone in Steal a Brainrot spawned a random brainrot each time the game reached 100,000 likes, and the count reset after each spawn. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Like_Goal_Milestone | id=C06-0167 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=high | checked=2026-11-07]
The Like Goal Milestone in Steal a Brainrot could not activate in private servers, and it was removed on March 21 and replaced with the Live Spawns board. Headless Horseman's change to OG rarity in Steal a Brainrot came from a poll, according to the Poll page. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Poll | id=C06-0169 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | event=2026-02-24 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Rarity word is stripped in the page; the Taco Tuesday page dates the change to February 24, 2026.]
Sammy's Suggestions hub on the Steal a Brainrot wiki has Feature Request, Improvement and Other forms for players to submit suggestions. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Suggestions | id=C06-0170 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=high | checked=2026-11-07]

## Gamepasses, Robux Shop and Roblox data

### Admin Panel commands
The Admin Panel in Steal a Brainrot has ten chat commands, typed with a semicolon, that the July 12, 2025 overhaul added and the wiki still lists: rocket, balloon, nightvision, control, jumpscare, ragdoll, inverse, jail, tiny and morph. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Admin_Panel | id=C14-0001 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | event=2025-07-12 | checked=2026-11-07 | also=https://apis.roblox.com/game-passes/v1/universes/7709344486/game-passes?passView=Full&pageSize=100 | note=The wiki says the overhaul raised the price from 1,999 to 4,999 Robux. Price is covered by the Admin Panel conflict record.]
The ;rocket command in Steal a Brainrot attaches a rocket to the targeted user and shoots them up into the sky, and players often pair it with ;jail once the user is at their highest point. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Admin_Panel | id=C14-0002 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
The ;balloon command in Steal a Brainrot makes the targeted user's head bigger for 15 seconds so they jump higher, and a nerf around July 21, 2025 made it impossible to balloon yourself while holding a Brainrot. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Admin_Panel | id=C14-0003 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | event=2025-07-21 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=The wiki gives the nerf as around July 21, 2025, with no exact date.]
The ;nightvision command in Steal a Brainrot lets the targeted user see invisible players for 1 minute by showing avatar limbs with red boxes. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Admin_Panel | id=C14-0004 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
The ;control command in Steal a Brainrot lets the user control the targeted user for 10 seconds, and it cannot be run on yourself. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Admin_Panel | id=C14-0005 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
The ;jumpscare command in Steal a Brainrot pops up Tim Cheese, and it was formerly Tung Tung Tung Sahur before that Brainrot was copyrighted. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Admin_Panel | id=C14-0006 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
The ;ragdoll command in Steal a Brainrot ragdolls the targeted user, either to stop them moving for a short time or to unequip any Brainrots they are moving or stealing. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Admin_Panel | id=C14-0007 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
The ;inverse command in Steal a Brainrot reverses the targeted user's controls for 10 seconds. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Admin_Panel | id=C14-0008 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
The ;jail command in Steal a Brainrot traps the targeted user inside a semi-transparent box for 10 seconds, though they can escape by cloning themselves and switching with the clone. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Admin_Panel | id=C14-0009 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
The ;tiny command in Steal a Brainrot makes the targeted user tiny for 30 seconds and makes them glide a bit when they stop moving. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Admin_Panel | id=C14-0010 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]
The ;morph command in Steal a Brainrot changes the targeted user's avatar into one of three Secret Brainrots for 1 minute: Tralalero Tralala, Ballerina Cappuccina or Bombardiro Crocodilo, chosen at random. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Admin_Panel | id=C14-0011 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | checked=2026-11-07]

## Records, business, merchandise and legal, more

### Concurrent player peaks and visits
In July 2025, Steal a Brainrot reached 7 billion visits and had a peak of 5 million concurrent players, according to Wikipedia. [source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steal_a_Brainrot | id=C10-0005 | type=secondary | status=unverified | confidence=medium | event=2025-07 | checked=2026-11-07 | also=https://massivelyop.com/2025/07/28/robloxs-latest-fad-minigame-is-designed-to-make-kids-absolutely-miserable/ | note=Wikipedia cites Massively Overpowered (2025-07-28) and Game Rant; neither was opened by the researcher.]
Steal a Brainrot's Fandom wiki lists its highest concurrent player count as 25,836,222 players, set in Update 20 on October 11, 2025. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Steal_a_Brainrot_(Game) | id=C10-0007 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | event=2025-10-11 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=This conflicts with the 25.4 million all-time October 2025 peak in PocketGamer.biz and the 25.2 million in Outlook Respawn. See the existing Needs review conflict.]
Before the August 2025 Admin War in Steal a Brainrot, Roblox's platform-wide concurrent user record was 32.69 million, set in July 2025, according to Wikipedia. [source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steal_a_Brainrot | id=C10-0008 | type=secondary | status=unverified | confidence=medium | event=2025-07 | checked=2026-11-07 | also=https://www.tubefilter.com/2025/08/25/roblox-grow-garden-steal-brainrot-admin-war-record/ | note=Wikipedia cites Tubefilter for this, which was not opened by the researcher.]
The Steal a Brainrot Bruno Mars concert drew a peak of 10 million livestream viewers, in addition to 12.8 million concurrent users, according to Wikipedia. [source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steal_a_Brainrot | id=C10-0009 | type=secondary | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-01-23 | event=2026-01-17 | checked=2026-11-07 | also=https://www.gamesindustry.biz/roblox-claims-bruno-mars-steal-a-brainrot-performance-drew-a-record-128-million-concurrent-users-issued-54-million-brainrot-collectibles | note=Wikipedia cites GamesIndustry.biz for this, which was not opened by the researcher.]
### Fortnite Steal the Brainrot (separate from the Roblox game)
In July 2025, the Fortnite Creative island Steal the Brainrot, which Epic Games licensed from Steal a Brainrot, peaked at about 400,000 concurrent players, breaking the earlier Fortnite Creative record of 235,000 set by Super Red vs Blue in May 2025. [source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steal_a_Brainrot | id=C10-0010 | type=secondary | status=unverified | confidence=medium | event=2025-07 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Fortnite version only. Wikipedia cites Pocket Tactics and GameSpot, which were not opened by the researcher.]
The Fortnite Creative island Steal the Brainrot reached 500,000 concurrent players on September 13, 2025, temporarily beating the Fortnite Battle Royale mode, according to Wikipedia. [source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steal_a_Brainrot | id=C10-0011 | type=secondary | status=unverified | confidence=medium | event=2025-09-13 | checked=2026-11-07 | also=https://www.polygon.com/fortnite-steal-a-brainrot-concurrents-peak-records-roblox-who-makes-it/ | note=Fortnite version only. The Sept 13 date and the Battle Royale comparison come from Wikipedia, which cites Gaming News and Polygon.]
Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney celebrated the success of the Fortnite Creative island Steal the Brainrot by retweeting posts about it in September 2025. [source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steal_a_Brainrot | id=C10-0012 | type=secondary | status=unverified | confidence=medium | event=2025-09 | checked=2026-11-07 | also=https://www.polygon.com/fortnite-steal-a-brainrot-concurrents-peak-records-roblox-who-makes-it/ | note=Fortnite version only.]
