### La Casa Boo
La Casa Boo in Steal a Brainrot translates from Spanish as The Boo House, but the name is meant to be The Spooky House. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Casa_Boo | id=B4-0284 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=The source uses curly quotes around The Boo House; it is the Spanish-to-English translation.]
La Casa Boo in Steal a Brainrot is meant to be The Spooky House, since boo is onomatopoeia for a shout or shriek that spooks. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Casa_Boo | id=B4-0285 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Translated from Italian, the name La Casa Boo in Steal a Brainrot means The House Boo. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Casa_Boo | id=B4-0286 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
In the Limited Trick or Treating event, La Casa Boo in Steal a Brainrot is the rarest Brainrot to encounter and gives the most Candy Corns, 50 of them. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Casa_Boo | id=B4-0287 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
One of the Divine La Casa Boo in Steal a Brainrot is from RustyNickle40 and has the Strawberry trait. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Casa_Boo | id=B4-0288 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
La Casa Boo in Steal a Brainrot is very similar to the Haunted Fuse. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Casa_Boo | id=B4-0289 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
La Casa Boo in Steal a Brainrot appears in the biggest house during the trick or treat event, makes the most money, and often gives the least candy. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Casa_Boo | id=B4-0290 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
La Casa Boo in Steal a Brainrot has only one eye, a mouth of sharp teeth with a large tongue, and bare legs with sharp claws. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Casa_Boo | id=B4-0291 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
La Casa Boo in Steal a Brainrot is holding a trick-or-treat bag filled with candy. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Casa_Boo | id=B4-0292 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
### La Cucaracha
La Cucaracha in Steal a Brainrot is translated as The Cockroach. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Cucaracha | id=B4-0293 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
A trait on La Cucaracha in Steal a Brainrot goes onto its hat instead of its body, and the wiki says this also happens on Lirilì Larilà, Boneca Ambalabu, Tric Trac Baraboom and Pipi Avocado. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Cucaracha | id=B4-0294 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=The trait's name is blank in the wikitext. The wiki links the hat behavior to eyes on the side of the head.]
### La Easter Grande
La Easter Grande in Steal a Brainrot had 150,000 in stock as a Limited Brainrot. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Easter_Grande | id=B4-0295 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
The head of Lirilì Larilà on La Easter Grande in Steal a Brainrot is purple, shaped like an egg, has no eyes and is chipped at the top right. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Easter_Grande | id=B4-0296 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
The tire of Boneca Ambalabu on La Easter Grande in Steal a Brainrot is reskinned as a blue egg with green stripes. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Easter_Grande | id=B4-0297 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
The head of Tralalero Tralala on La Easter Grande in Steal a Brainrot is an egg-yellow arm instead of its usual blue. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Easter_Grande | id=B4-0298 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Bunny Bunny Bunny Sahur on La Easter Grande in Steal a Brainrot holds a basket of colored Easter eggs, and a baby chicken lays on top of it. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Easter_Grande | id=B4-0299 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
A baby chicken lays on top of Bunny Bunny Bunny Sahur on La Easter Grande in Steal a Brainrot, in place of the face of Boneca Ambalabu and the clock of Lirilì Larilà. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Easter_Grande | id=B4-0300 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
La Easter Grande in Steal a Brainrot is crafted in the Taco Truck from 1x Tictac Sahur, 1x Noo my Eggs and 1x La Grande Combinasion. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Easter_Grande | id=B4-0301 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
La Easter Grande in Steal a Brainrot is the first seasonal La Grande Combinasion reskin with an official Tung Tung Tung Sahur reskin. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Easter_Grande | id=B4-0302 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
La Easter Grande in Steal a Brainrot is the first seasonal reskin whose Tralalero Tralala does not match the reskin, using Bunny Tralala, which was released after it. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Easter_Grande | id=B4-0303 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
As of March 31, 2026, La Easter Grande in Steal a Brainrot was the second best Limited Quantity Brainrot. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Easter_Grande | id=B4-0304 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | event=2026-03-31 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=The wiki says it passed another Brainrot by $5M/s; that Brainrot's name is blank in the wikitext.]
La Easter Grande in Steal a Brainrot is the second best Limited Quantity seasonal reskin of La Grande Combinasion. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Easter_Grande | id=B4-0305 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
La Easter Grande in Steal a Brainrot is one of only three Brainrots whose stats were known before release, along with Ginger Gerat and Cerberus. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Easter_Grande | id=B4-0306 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
La Easter Grande in Steal a Brainrot shares animations with La Lucky Grande. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Easter_Grande | id=B4-0307 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Sammy (SpyderSammy) restocked 50K La Easter Grande in the Taco Truck during the Update 45 Admin Abuse, and it sold out almost immediately. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Easter_Grande | id=B4-0308 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
La Easter Grande in Steal a Brainrot shares the same stats as Caylusaurus, Steakini Fattini, Hopilikalika Hopilikalako and Antonio, before Antonio's second buff. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Easter_Grande | id=B4-0309 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
### La Extinct Grande
La Extinct Grande in Steal a Brainrot was obtained from the archeologist in the Extinct Event while it had stock. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Extinct_Grande | id=B4-0310 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
La Extinct Grande in Steal a Brainrot is crafted from 1x Extinct Ballerina, 1x Extinct Tralalero and 1x Extinct Matteo. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Extinct_Grande | id=B4-0311 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
The bat of Tung Tung Tung Sahur on La Extinct Grande in Steal a Brainrot is replaced with a spiked bone-mace. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Extinct_Grande | id=B4-0312 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=The character is blank in the wikitext; Tung Tung Tung Sahur is the bat carrier by its design.]
Boneca Ambalabu on La Extinct Grande in Steal a Brainrot has half its head turned into bone, and its wheel turned into a ribcage. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Extinct_Grande | id=B4-0313 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Some of Trippi Troppi's gills on La Extinct Grande in Steal a Brainrot turned into bone. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Extinct_Grande | id=B4-0314 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
La Extinct Grande in Steal a Brainrot originally had 500,000 in stock, and after a player bought one and it was refilled, it had 500,001. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Extinct_Grande | id=B4-0315 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
After La Extinct Grande in Steal a Brainrot sold out, 350,000 more were put back into stock, bringing the total to 850,001. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Extinct_Grande | id=B4-0316 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
La Extinct Grande is the first Limited Quantity Brainrot in Steal a Brainrot. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Extinct_Grande | id=B4-0317 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
La Extinct Grande and La Anniversary Grande are the only La Grande Combinasion reskins in Steal a Brainrot that are not based on a seasonal event. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Extinct_Grande | id=B4-0318 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
The original name of La Extinct Grande in Steal a Brainrot was La Extinct Combinasion. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Extinct_Grande | id=B4-0319 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
La Extinct Grande in Steal a Brainrot is the first La Grande Combinasion reskin that is not related to any Summer event. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Extinct_Grande | id=B4-0320 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
### La Food Combinasion
La Food Combinasion in Steal a Brainrot was teased by Sammy (SpyderSammy) in the Community Server before its release in Update 39 on February 21, 2026. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Food_Combinasion | id=B4-0321 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-31 | event=2026-02-21 | checked=2026-11-07]
In La Food Combinasion in Steal a Brainrot, Burguro is below the structure and Fryuro sits on top of Burguro. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Food_Combinasion | id=B4-0322 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-31 | checked=2026-11-07]
La Food Combinasion in Steal a Brainrot has about a 0.3% chance from the Taco Lucky Block. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Food_Combinasion | id=B4-0323 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-31 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Conflicts with the 0.1% figure in the existing database; see open notes.]
La Food Combinasion in Steal a Brainrot is the rarest Brainrot in the Taco Lucky Block, according to the wiki. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Food_Combinasion | id=B4-0324 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-31 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Same 0.3% vs 0.1% conflict as the chance fact.]
La Food Combinasion in Steal a Brainrot was requested by many fans for some time before it was added. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Food_Combinasion | id=B4-0325 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-31 | checked=2026-11-07]
The materials of La Food Combinasion in Steal a Brainrot add up to $242.5M/s of income, which is far more than the $90M/s it makes. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Food_Combinasion | id=B4-0326 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-31 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=The wiki's arithmetic from the materials' incomes: 42.5M + 50M + 150M.]
Burguro And Fryuro in Steal a Brainrot makes $60M/s more than La Food Combinasion, which is built from it. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Food_Combinasion | id=B4-0327 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-31 | checked=2026-11-07]
La Food Combinasion in Steal a Brainrot's materials had Yin Yang-looking Garama and Madundung in the leak, but this was a glass effect and texture missing from the leak images. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Food_Combinasion | id=B4-0328 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-31 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Leak. The wiki explains the look as glass missing in leak images.]
La Food Combinasion in Steal a Brainrot is the only Taco Lucky Block Brainrot without Mexican design elements; its parts are based on burger, French fries, ketchup, mustard, salt and honey. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Food_Combinasion | id=B4-0329 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-31 | checked=2026-11-07]
La Food Combinasion in Steal a Brainrot makes less than its materials, similar to La Supreme Combinasion before it was buffed to $200M/s. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Food_Combinasion | id=B4-0330 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-31 | checked=2026-11-07]
### La Fuse Machine
La Fuse Machine in Steal a Brainrot is the second Brainrot based on a game mechanic, after Sammyni Fattini, which is based on the Fat Sammy event. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Fuse_Machine | id=B4-0331 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-26 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=The wiki's sentence is confusing: it names the Fuse Machine itself as the mechanic.]
La Fuse Machine in Steal a Brainrot has the same stats as Los Admins and La Secret Combinasion after its nerf. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Fuse_Machine | id=B4-0332 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-26 | checked=2026-11-07]
La Fuse Machine's leaked preview in Steal a Brainrot showed it at $115M/s, but it was nerfed to $95M/s when the update came out. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Fuse_Machine | id=B4-0333 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-26 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Leak in the official Discord server.]
La Fuse Machine in Steal a Brainrot can be obtained from Sammy's Code as well as from the RNG Machine. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Fuse_Machine | id=B4-0334 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-26 | checked=2026-11-07]
### La Ginger Sekolah
La Ginger Sekolah in Steal a Brainrot was teased in the official community server. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Ginger_Sekolah | id=B4-0335 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
La Ginger Sekolah in Steal a Brainrot is the Christmas version of Esok Sekolah and the second reskin of it, after La Casa Boo. La Ginger Sekolah, La Casa Boo and Esok Sekolah in Steal a Brainrot all share the same walking animation. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Ginger_Sekolah | id=B4-0337 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
The bell on La Ginger Sekolah in Steal a Brainrot does not move and does not produce soundwave particles, unlike the bell on Esok Sekolah. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Ginger_Sekolah | id=B4-0338 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
La Ginger Sekolah in Steal a Brainrot looks the same as Esok Sekolah, but is made of gingerbread instead of wood, with a vanilla frosting outline. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Ginger_Sekolah | id=B4-0339 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]

The middle of La Grande Combinasion in Steal a Brainrot has Boneca Ambalabu's body on the left and Tung Tung Tung Sahur's body on the right. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Grande_Combinasion | id=B4-0340 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-07 | checked=2026-11-07]
Tralalero Tralala sticks out of Boneca Ambalabu's body in La Grande Combinasion in Steal a Brainrot. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Grande_Combinasion | id=B4-0341 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-07 | checked=2026-11-07]
La Grande Combinasion in Steal a Brainrot can be obtained from the Admin Lucky Block with a 0.5% (1 in 200) chance. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Grande_Combinasion | id=B4-0342 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-07 | checked=2026-11-07]
La Grande Combinasion in Steal a Brainrot has the most obtainment methods of any Brainrot, at 8 ways. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Grande_Combinasion | id=B4-0343 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-07 | checked=2026-11-07]
La Grande Combinasion in Steal a Brainrot can be obtained from the Jump for Eggs LTM. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Grande_Combinasion | id=B4-0344 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-07 | checked=2026-11-07]
La Grande Combinasion in Steal a Brainrot can be crafted from the Brainrot Trader from 1x Rang Ring Bus and 1x Chicleteira Bicicleteira, among other recipes. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Grande_Combinasion | id=B4-0345 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-07 | checked=2026-11-07]
La Grande Combinasion in Steal a Brainrot was leaked by Sammy on June 19, 2025, making it the first leaked Brainrot. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Grande_Combinasion | id=B4-0346 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-07 | event=2025-06-19 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=The wiki gives both 06/19/25 and July 19 2025; the date conflicts. See open notes.]
The original name of La Grande Combinasion in Steal a Brainrot on leak was La Grande Combinazione, which is why the Tung Tung Tung Sahur sound says CombinaZIONE. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Grande_Combinasion | id=B4-0347 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-07 | checked=2026-11-07]
The full name of La Grande Combinasion in Steal a Brainrot is Trippa Troppa Tralala Lirilira Tung Tung Sahur Boneca Tung Tung Tralalero Trippa Troppa Crocodina. La Grande Combinasion's full name in Steal a Brainrot ends with the last name Bombardiro Crocodilo, although Bombardiro Crocodilo is not in its design. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Grande_Combinasion | id=B4-0349 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-07 | checked=2026-11-07]
Garama and Madundung in Steal a Brainrot, added in Update 06, took over from La Grande Combinasion as the best Brainrot, making $40M/s more while costing $9B more. La Grande Combinasion in Steal a Brainrot turned one year old on July 21. La Grande Combinasion is the only Brainrot obtained from a Lucky Block that is a requirement for Rebirth in Steal a Brainrot. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Grande_Combinasion | id=B4-0353 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-07 | checked=2026-11-07]
Los Nooo My Hotspotsitos in Steal a Brainrot makes $5.5M/s and costs $1B, the same cost as La Grande Combinasion. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Grande_Combinasion | id=B4-0354 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-07 | checked=2026-11-07]

La Jolly Grande in Steal a Brainrot was released on December 6, 2025 at 3:00 PM EST with Santa's Fuse. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Jolly_Grande | id=B4-0355 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | event=2025-12-06 | checked=2026-11-07]

[source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Jolly_Grande | id=B4-0356 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]

[source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/La_Supreme_Combinasion | id=B4-0427 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-08-16 | checked=2026-11-07]

Lerulerulerule in Steal a Brainrot is an anthropomorphized cactus with a penguin head, a cowboy hat, boots and belted denim shorts. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Lerulerulerule | id=B4-0500 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-08-25 | checked=2026-11-07]
Lerulerulerule in Steal a Brainrot spawns more often than most Mythic Brainrots, possibly because its Red Carpet RoadWeight was set to 0.705 instead of the intended 0.075. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Lerulerulerule | id=B4-0501 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-08-25 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=The wiki calls the RoadWeight cause the most likely reason.]
Lerulerulerule in Steal a Brainrot is more common than most Legendary and Epic Brainrots, according to player surveys cited by the wiki. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Lerulerulerule | id=B4-0502 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-08-25 | checked=2026-11-07]
The real name of Lerulerulerule in Steal a Brainrot is Penguinelli Cactussini, but it was changed for an unknown reason. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Lerulerulerule | id=B4-0503 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-08-25 | checked=2026-11-07]
### License
Sammy said he currently cannot get the license needed to add Smurf Cat to Steal a Brainrot. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Smurf_Cat | id=B7-0280 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-06 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Wiki claim; not confirmed by a Sammy post.]
### Lionel Cactuseli
Lionel Cactuseli in Steal a Brainrot has about a 0.396% spawn chance on the Red Carpet, which is 6 out of 1515. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Lionel_Cactuseli | id=B4-0505 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-09-27 | checked=2026-11-07]
Lionel Cactuseli is one of only two lion Brainrots in Steal a Brainrot, the other being Lionello Casarello. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Lionel_Cactuseli | id=B4-0506 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-09-27 | checked=2026-11-07]
Lionel Cactuseli in Steal a Brainrot is credited to @alexey_pigeon as its creator in the infobox. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Lionel_Cactuseli | id=B4-0507 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-09-27 | checked=2026-11-07]
### Lionello Casarello
Lionello Casarello in Steal a Brainrot has a delightful expression with two small sharp teeth and slightly raised eyebrows. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Lionello_Casarello | id=B4-0508 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-06 | checked=2026-11-07]
Lionello Casarello is the second lion Brainrot in Steal a Brainrot, after Lionel Cactuseli. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Lionello_Casarello | id=B4-0509 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-06 | checked=2026-11-07]
Lionello Casarello in Steal a Brainrot is a worse reskin of Bearito Cabinito, making only 58.5M. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Lionello_Casarello | id=B4-0510 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-06 | checked=2026-11-07]
The Casa in the name Lionello Casarello in Steal a Brainrot means house in Spanish. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Lionello_Casarello | id=B4-0511 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-06 | checked=2026-11-07]
Lionello Casarello in Steal a Brainrot has a released exist count of only 1196, so the wiki expects Sammy (SpyderSammy) to buff it. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Lionello_Casarello | id=B4-0512 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-06 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=The buff expectation is the wiki's speculation.]
### Lirilì Larilà
Lirilì Larilà in Steal a Brainrot is a Common Brainrot that appears second in the Index. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Lirilì_Larilà | id=B4-0513 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-08-31 | checked=2026-11-07]
Lirilì Larilà in Steal a Brainrot has a flying clock in its idle animation, but not elsewhere. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Lirilì_Larilà | id=B4-0514 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-08-31 | checked=2026-11-07]
The original concept art of Lirilì Larilà in Steal a Brainrot had a clock floating above its head, which the game only shows during its idle animation or in La Grande Combinasion. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Lirilì_Larilà | id=B4-0515 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-08-31 | checked=2026-11-07]
The clock of Lirilì Larilà in Steal a Brainrot sits inside its body, which you can see by zooming into the model. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Lirilì_Larilà | id=B4-0516 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-08-31 | checked=2026-11-07]
Lirilì Larilà is the only Common Brainrot in Steal a Brainrot that shows up in La Grande Combinasion. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Lirilì_Larilà | id=B4-0517 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-08-31 | checked=2026-11-07]
Lirilì Larilà is the only Brainrot in Steal a Brainrot with tone marks in its name. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Lirilì_Larilà | id=B4-0518 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-08-31 | checked=2026-11-07]
A Lirilì Larilà with the Strawberry trait in Steal a Brainrot looks like Strawberry Elephant. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Lirilì_Larilà | id=B4-0519 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-08-31 | checked=2026-11-07]
Lirilì Larilà in Steal a Brainrot costs 10 times more than Noobini Pizzanini but makes only 3 times more income. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Lirilì_Larilà | id=B4-0520 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-08-31 | checked=2026-11-07]
Lirilì Larilà is found in La Karkerkar Combinasion in Steal a Brainrot, along with La Grande Combinasion. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Lirilì_Larilà | id=B4-0521 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-08-31 | checked=2026-11-07]
Lirilì Larilà in Steal a Brainrot is credited to capybarawt as its creator in the infobox. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Lirilì_Larilà | id=B4-0522 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-08-31 | checked=2026-11-07]
### List List List Sahur
List List List Sahur in Steal a Brainrot has a joyful smile, red cheeks, and a mix of light green and red coloring. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/List_List_List_Sahur | id=B5-0001 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
List List List Sahur in Steal a Brainrot has an appearance similar to Job Job Job Sahur. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/List_List_List_Sahur | id=B5-0002 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
List List List Sahur in Steal a Brainrot holds a list naming Strawberry Elephant, Dragon Cannelloni, Garama and Madundung, Spaghetti Tualetti and Meowl, which is its wish list. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/List_List_List_Sahur | id=B5-0003 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
List List List Sahur in Steal a Brainrot was the hardest to obtain of the four Christmas Event Brainrots. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/List_List_List_Sahur | id=B5-0004 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
List List List Sahur in Steal a Brainrot was used to craft the limited La Jolly Grande. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/List_List_List_Sahur | id=B5-0005 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
List List List Sahur in Steal a Brainrot has the same income and price as La Sahur Combinasion and Telemorte. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/List_List_List_Sahur | id=B5-0006 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
List List List Sahur in Steal a Brainrot was not in the Brainrot Express, even though it is a Christmas themed Brainrot. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/List_List_List_Sahur | id=B5-0007 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
List List List Sahur in Steal a Brainrot was added on December 6, 2025 at 3 PM EST along with Santa's Fuse. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/List_List_List_Sahur | id=B5-0008 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | event=2025-12-06 | checked=2026-11-07]
List List List Sahur in Steal a Brainrot can rarely spawn from the Winter Hour event. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/List_List_List_Sahur | id=B5-0009 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]

### Los 25
The middle Los 25 in Steal a Brainrot has blue eyes, the left one has golden eyes, and the right one has purple eyes. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_25 | id=B5-0010 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Los 25 in Steal a Brainrot is the only multi-member Brainrot whose members have different eye colors but no different expressions. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_25 | id=B5-0011 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Los Tortus and Hydra Dragon Cannelloni also have different eye colors per member, but they show different expressions.]
Los 25 in Steal a Brainrot is the first Los variant to be obtainable before its main version, 25, because the Festive Lucky Block and North Pole Event were accessible before December 25, 2025. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_25 | id=B5-0012 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Page writes the date as 25/12/2025.]
Los 25 in Steal a Brainrot has the same income as La Grande Combinasion but costs $500M more. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_25 | id=B5-0013 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Los 25 in Steal a Brainrot can be obtained from the Festive Lucky Block and from Santa's Factory. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_25 | id=B5-0014 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
### Los 67
Los 67 in Steal a Brainrot was released on October 4, 2025 with the Los Lucky Blocks. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_67 | id=B5-0015 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | event=2025-10-04 | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot, the middle Los 67 is blushing and making the famous 67 hand gesture with a happy expression. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_67 | id=B5-0016 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot, the right Los 67 is in a fighting stance with a tough expression, and the left Los 67 looks tired or sad. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_67 | id=B5-0017 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Los 67 in Steal a Brainrot was nerfed from $22.5M/s to $13.5M/s, a cut of about 40 percent, for a reason the wiki does not explain. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_67 | id=B5-0018 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Page says the nerf reason is unknown; 40% is the page's own figure.]
Before its nerf, Los 67 in Steal a Brainrot made exactly three times the income of its parent 67, which made $7.5M/s, making it one of the few accurate Los Brainrots. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_67 | id=B5-0019 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Los 67 in Steal a Brainrot has a 0.5% chance from the Los Lucky Blocks, but still makes less than Los Combinasionas, which makes $15M/s with a 1% chance. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_67 | id=B5-0020 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Los 67 was the best Brainrot from the Los Lucky Blocks in Steal a Brainrot for a long time, until Los Sekolahs was added. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_67 | id=B5-0021 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
### Los Admins
Los Admins in Steal a Brainrot can be crafted at the Los Traders from one Sammyni Fattini and one Los Fruits, from one Sammyni Cakini, or from one Steakini Fattini, one Caylusaurus and one Los Spyderinis. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Admins | id=B5-0022 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-05 | checked=2026-11-07]
Los Admins is the first appearance of baby versions of Steakini Fattini, Sammyni Fattini, and Caylusaurus in Steal a Brainrot. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Admins | id=B5-0023 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-05 | checked=2026-11-07]
Los Admins in Steal a Brainrot represents the people who hosted Admin Abuse, which were Steak, Caylus, and Sammy (SpyderSammy). [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Admins | id=B5-0024 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-05 | checked=2026-11-07]
Rusty, who hosted Taco Tuesday, is not part of Los Admins in Steal a Brainrot. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Admins | id=B5-0025 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-05 | checked=2026-11-07]
In the idle animation of Los Admins in Steal a Brainrot, baby Steakini Fattini tries to steal baby Sammyni Fattini's taco. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Admins | id=B5-0026 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-05 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=The page reads this as a hint that Steakini Fattini is the greediest of the three Admins.]
### Los Amigos
Los Amigos in Steal a Brainrot has heart-shaped pink eyes on its Los Mariachis skeleton half and wears a sombrero with two moccasins. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Amigos | id=B5-0028 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
The name Los Amigos in Steal a Brainrot is Spanish for friends. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Amigos | id=B5-0029 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Los Amigos in Steal a Brainrot shares its obtain chance with Hydra Bunny and is rarer than Rosey and Teddy. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Amigos | id=B5-0030 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Los Amigos was the original name of Los Mobilis in Steal a Brainrot, and the name was later given to a different Brainrot. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Amigos | id=B5-0031 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07 | also=https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Mobilis | note=The Los Mobilis page says its original creator was @gaelitod0 on TikTok.]
Los Amigos is the highest money-making baby duo in Steal a Brainrot, surpassing Los Primos by $99M/s. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Amigos | id=B5-0032 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
### Los Bombinitos
Los Bombinitos in Steal a Brainrot are three white happy geese flying with turbines. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Bombinitos | id=B5-0033 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-03 | checked=2026-11-07]
Los Bombinitos in Steal a Brainrot makes more money than Los Tungtungtungcitos but has a higher chance in the Los Lucky Blocks than Los Tungtungtungcitos. Los Bombinitos is one of the few Los Brainrots in Steal a Brainrot whose members all share the same facial expression. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Bombinitos | id=B5-0035 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-03 | checked=2026-11-07]
The left Los Bombinito in Steal a Brainrot has its eyes glitched out in the model. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Bombinitos | id=B5-0036 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-03 | checked=2026-11-07]
Los Bombinitos used to appear in the old Sammy's Base in Steal a Brainrot. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Bombinitos | id=B5-0037 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-03 | checked=2026-11-07]
### Los Bros
Los Bros in Steal a Brainrot was originally made by @italianbrainrotma75 on TikTok on August 2, before it was released in the game. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Bros | id=B5-0038 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Year not stated on the page.]
Los Bros in Steal a Brainrot received a nerf on September 13 that cut its cost from $6B to $2.6B and its income from $37.5M/s to $24M/s. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Bros | id=B5-0039 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Year of the nerf is not stated on the page.]
The Los Bros crafting recipe in Steal a Brainrot was reduced from needing two Los Combinasionas to needing only one. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Bros | id=B5-0040 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Los Bros had the same stats as Tictac Sahur in Steal a Brainrot before it was nerfed. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Bros | id=B5-0041 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Los Bros in Steal a Brainrot is made from one Los Tralalerito and one Los Tungtungtungcito, not three of each. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Bros | id=B5-0042 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Los Bros is the second rarest Craft Machine Brainrot in Steal a Brainrot, after Tralaledon. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Bros | id=B5-0043 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=The page says Tralaledon was first because its recipe uses carpet only Nuclearo Dinossauro.]
In Steal a Brainrot the happy Tralalerito in Los Bros emits a blue aura, while the happy Tungtungtungcito emits an orange aura. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Bros | id=B5-0044 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
### Los Bunitos
Los Bunitos took four months to get a Los version after its parent Bunito Bunito Spinito in Steal a Brainrot. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Bunitos | id=B5-0045 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Los Bunitos in Steal a Brainrot is the first event-exclusive variant of a Brainrot that is also event-exclusive on a different event, since Bunito Bunito Spinito is a New Year's Machine exclusive. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Bunitos | id=B5-0046 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]

The 1x1x1x1 and Guest 666 Brainrots in Steal a Brainrot were released before Los Hackers. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Hackers | id=B5-0129 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
The baby John Doe in Los Hackers in Steal a Brainrot is frowning, unlike the adult John Doe. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Hackers | id=B5-0130 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
### Los Hotspotsitos
Los Hotspotsitos in Steal a Brainrot was released on 8/1/25 according to the wiki, which uses day/month order elsewhere. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Hotspotsitos | id=B5-0131 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Date format ambiguous. Wiki writes 25/12/2025 elsewhere, so 8/1/25 may mean 8 January 2025. Not converted.]
Los Hotspotsitos in Steal a Brainrot could be obtained by rolling it out of the Fuse Machine with a relatively low chance. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Hotspotsitos | id=B5-0132 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
When Los Hotspotsitos was leaked in Steal a Brainrot, it was theorized to come from the Pot Hotspot Ritual, but that ritual was later removed and the theory was disproven. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Hotspotsitos | id=B5-0133 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Los Hotspotsitos was originally planned to be named Los Hotspots in Steal a Brainrot. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Hotspotsitos | id=B5-0134 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot the middle Los Hotspotsito is happy, the left one is disgruntled, and the right one is sad. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Hotspotsitos | id=B5-0135 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
### Los Jobcitos
Los Jobcitos in Steal a Brainrot was created by @gullie_0_o, according to the infobox. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Jobcitos | id=B5-0136 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Los Jobcitos and Los 67 were the only two new Brainrots that were not added before the initial Los Lucky Blocks release in Steal a Brainrot. In Steal a Brainrot the left Los Jobcito is sad, the middle one is happy, and the right one is mad or upset. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Jobcitos | id=B5-0138 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
The Los Jobcitos in Steal a Brainrot have white bats, while adult Job Job Job Sahur has light brown bats. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Jobcitos | id=B5-0139 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Los Jobcitos in Steal a Brainrot shares its exact stats with Tung Tung Tung Sahur. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Jobcitos | id=B5-0140 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
When Tung Tung Tung Sahur was removed the second time in Steal a Brainrot, Los Jobcitos was not used as its replacement, unlike the first removal, which Gangster Footera replaced. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Jobcitos | id=B5-0141 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
### Los Jolly Combinasionas
Los Jolly Combinasionas in Steal a Brainrot could be bought from Santa's Shop for Gold Elves or Robux. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Jolly_Combinasionas | id=B5-0142 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]

Los Karkeritos was released in Steal a Brainrot on October 4, 2025 along with the Yin Yang event and the Los Lucky Blocks. Los Karkeritos has the same price and income as Las Vaquitas Saturnitas in Steal a Brainrot, and both rituals use a $325K/s Brainrot. ### Los Mobilis
Los Mobilis in Steal a Brainrot was not originally created by Sammy; its original name was Los Amigos, and its original creator was @gaelitod0 on TikTok. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Mobilis | id=B5-0174 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07 | also=https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Amigos | note=Los Amigos page gives the same name link: Los Amigos was the original name of Los Mobilis.]
The name Los Mobilis in Steal a Brainrot comes from translating The Mobiles into Spanish, but the correct Spanish is Los Moviles. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Mobilis | id=B5-0175 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Los Mobilis was the first Multiple Brainrot in Steal a Brainrot to include two special Brainrots, one from the exclusive Taco Lucky Block and one from the original Fuse Machine. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Mobilis | id=B5-0176 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Los Mobilis, Pinealotto Fruttarino, Frio Ninja, Snailenzo and Tentacolo Tecnico are the only Brainrots in the Witch Fuse of Steal a Brainrot with nothing to do with Halloween. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Mobilis | id=B5-0177 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Los Mobilis was the last Tier II Secret in the Steal a Brainrot Fuse Machine with income above $15M/s, until it was nerfed to $8.5M/s. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Mobilis | id=B5-0178 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Los Mobilis in Steal a Brainrot has two 1 of 1 mutations, Cursed and Cyber. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Mobilis | id=B5-0179 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot the right side of Los Mobilis is Los Nooo My Hotspotsitos, a mini burrito with limbs holding a phone, and the left side is Los Hotspotsitos, a mini skeleton with a phone as its head. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Mobilis | id=B5-0180 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]

Los Planitos is the first duo Brainrot in Steal a Brainrot with a female and a male, since it pairs a Las Vaquitas Saturnitas with a baby Bisonte Giuppitere. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Planitos | id=B5-0209 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Los Planitos in Steal a Brainrot has a baby Bisonte Giuppitere, even though no separate baby version of Bisonte Giuppitere exists. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Planitos | id=B5-0210 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
The baby Bisonte Giuppitere in Los Planitos has four cow legs instead of two human legs, like the adult Bisonte Giuppitere. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Planitos | id=B5-0211 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
When Los Planitos was revealed in Steal a Brainrot, many players thought its baby Bisonte Giuppitere could have been a baby Blackhole Goat. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Planitos | id=B5-0212 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Los Planitos shares the same stats as Snailo Clovero in Steal a Brainrot. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Planitos | id=B5-0213 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Los Planitos can be traded from the Brainrot Trader in Steal a Brainrot with 1x Mariachi Corazoni, 1x Nooo My Hotspot and 1x Perrito Burrito, or with 2x Los Burritos. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Planitos | id=B5-0214 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
### Los Primos
Los Primos in Steal a Brainrot was added on September 27, 2025 with the Craft Machine update. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Primos | id=B5-0215 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | event=2025-09-27 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=CONFLICT: the database already says Update 25 in November 2025. Page infobox says release=Update 25.]
Los Primos was the best Brainrot craftable in the Craft Machine in Steal a Brainrot before the February 28, 2026 buff. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Primos | id=B5-0216 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Los Primos means The Cousin in Spanish or Portuguese, and the name also refers to the shark and orca it is based on, the primary animals of the sea food chain. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Primos | id=B5-0217 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Los Primos in Steal a Brainrot is based on a shark, the Los Tralalerito, and an orca, the Los Orcalito. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Primos | id=B5-0218 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Los Primos was the last Brainrot Sammy added to the Craft Machine in Steal a Brainrot before the machine was removed. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Primos | id=B5-0219 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Los Primos requires a 67 to craft in Steal a Brainrot. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Primos | id=B5-0220 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Los Primos was crafted in the Craft Machine in Steal a Brainrot from Los Orcalitos, Los Tralaleritos, a 67 and Los Bros. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Primos | id=B5-0221 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Only two players have a Phantom Los Primos in Steal a Brainrot, because the Phantom mutation is only obtainable on Los Primos through fishing. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Primos | id=B5-0222 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
### Los Puggies
Los Puggies in Steal a Brainrot was teased by Sammy on November 5, 2025 at 12:08 PM EST. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Puggies | id=B5-0223 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | event=2025-11-05 | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot the right Los Puggy is excited and sticking its tongue out, the middle one looks normal, and the left one is sad. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Puggies | id=B5-0224 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Los Puggies was initially meant to be Money Meow in Steal a Brainrot, a cat counterpart for Money Money Puggy. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Puggies | id=B5-0225 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Los Puggies was used in a Los Traders recipe for Moby Bros in Steal a Brainrot. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Puggies | id=B5-0226 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Los Puggies in Steal a Brainrot got a buff, unknown to most players, from $30M/s to $40M/s. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Puggies | id=B5-0227 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Los Puggies in Steal a Brainrot was made permanently reobtainable in the new Money Money Puggy ritual. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Puggies | id=B5-0228 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Los Puggies could be obtained three ways in Steal a Brainrot: from the Brainrot Dealer, from the Brainrot Trader, and from the Money Money Puggy ritual. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Puggies | id=B5-0229 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Los Puggies can be crafted in the Brainrot Trader in Steal a Brainrot from 2x Mariachi Corazoni and 1x Los Nooo My Hotspotsitos, from 1x Los 67 and 1x Los Chicleteiras, or from 1x Money Money Puggy and 1x 67. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Puggies | id=B5-0230 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
### Los Quesadillas
Los Quesadillas in Steal a Brainrot came out on November 18, 2025. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Quesadillas | id=B5-0231 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | event=2025-11-18 | checked=2026-11-07]

### Los Secret Combinasionas
Sammy said only 2,000 to 3,000 units of Los Secret Combinasionas should be in stock in Steal a Brainrot, which makes it as rare as a Sammyini Cakini. Los Secret Combinasionas in Steal a Brainrot has the same stats as Burguro And Fryuro. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Secret_Combinasionas | id=B5-0235 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Los Secret Combinasionas is not used in any recipe in Steal a Brainrot, even though it is a Los version of La Secret Combinasion. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Secret_Combinasionas | id=B5-0236 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Los Secret Combinasionas is the fifth Brainrot from the Secret Lucky Block to get a Los variant in Steal a Brainrot, after Los Hotspotsitos, Los Tortus, Los Spaghettis and Los Sekolahs. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Secret_Combinasionas | id=B5-0237 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Los Secret Combinasionas uses a much sadder Los Hotspotsitos than the original, and almost all of its parts show negative emotions except Los Spaghettis. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Secret_Combinasionas | id=B5-0238 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Los Secret Combinasionas in Steal a Brainrot has a Los Sekolah on the left, a Los Tortus on the right, a Los Spaghetti in the center, and a Los Hotspotsitos head on top of the Spaghetti. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Secret_Combinasionas | id=B5-0239 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Los Secret Combinasionas in Steal a Brainrot has an adult Tortuginni shell on the back of its Los Spaghetti. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Secret_Combinasionas | id=B5-0240 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Los Secret Combinasionas can be crafted at the Los Traders in Steal a Brainrot from Los Sekolahs and Spaghetti Tualetti, or from La Food Combinasion, Spaghetti Tualetti and Esok Sekolah. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Secret_Combinasionas | id=B5-0241 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
### Los Sekolahs
Los Sekolahs has a 0.25% chance from the Los Lucky Blocks in Steal a Brainrot, so about 400 or more Los Lucky Blocks need to be opened to get one. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Sekolahs | id=B5-0242 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Los Sekolahs is the fourth Brainrot from the Secret Lucky Block to get a Los variant in Steal a Brainrot, after Los Hotspotsitos, Los Tortus and Los Spaghettis. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Sekolahs | id=B5-0243 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Los Sekolahs makes $110M/s in Steal a Brainrot, more than Los Spaghettis at $70M/s, even though Spaghetti Tualetti is rarer than Esok Sekolah. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Sekolahs | id=B5-0244 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
The Plants Vs Brainrots version of Los Sekolahs was called Los Sekolitos, and it was replaced by Los Casettatatatata before Los Sekolahs was added to Steal a Brainrot. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Sekolahs | id=B5-0245 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Los Sekolahs was leaked more than 26 days before its release in Steal a Brainrot, the second longest wait after Cola Cat. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Sekolahs | id=B5-0246 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Wiki says it was leaked by a name that is missing from the text. Cola Cat leak to release is said to be the longest.]
Los Sekolahs has two 1 of 1 versions in Steal a Brainrot, Eclipse and Radioactive, and the Radioactive one also has the sun trait. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Sekolahs | id=B5-0247 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Los Sekolahs in Steal a Brainrot has a tongue sticking out and carries a sign with the number 9 on it. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Sekolahs | id=B5-0248 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot the right Los Sekolah has a scheming face, the middle one is smiling and happy, and the left one is crying. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Sekolahs | id=B5-0249 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]

### Lucky Blocks
The name Lucky Block in Steal a Brainrot comes from the Super Mario Bros franchise, where lucky blocks give random items when hit. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Lucky_Blocks | id=B5-0355 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-09-17 | checked=2026-11-07]

[source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Lucky_Blocks | id=B5-0357 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-09-17 | checked=2026-11-07]

[source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Lucky_Blocks | id=B5-0358 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-09-17 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Only 'late February 2026' is given by the page, so the event date is not exact.]
In late February 2026 Sammy added Los Sekolahs to the Los Admin Blocks in Steal a Brainrot at a 0.25% chance. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Lucky_Blocks | id=B5-0359 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-09-17 | checked=2026-11-07]
In late February 2026 Sammy added Los Amigos to the Los Taco Blocks in Steal a Brainrot at a 0.15% chance. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Lucky_Blocks | id=B5-0360 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-09-17 | checked=2026-11-07]
In late February 2026 Sammy added La Food Combinasion to a Lucky Block in Steal a Brainrot at a 0.1% chance. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Lucky_Blocks | id=B5-0361 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-09-17 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=The page does not name which block La Food Combinasion was added to.]
Los Lucky Blocks were the first baby-themed Lucky Block in Steal a Brainrot. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Lucky_Blocks | id=B5-0362 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-09-17 | checked=2026-11-07]
Placing a Lucky Block on the Witch Fuse in Steal a Brainrot hides its icon. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Lucky_Blocks | id=B5-0363 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-09-17 | checked=2026-11-07]
Rosey and Teddy has the rarest chance of any Brainrot that comes from a Lucky Block in Steal a Brainrot. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Lucky_Blocks | id=B5-0364 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-09-17 | checked=2026-11-07]
The Admin Lucky Block, Los Lucky Blocks and Festive Lucky Block were available in the Advent Calendar in Steal a Brainrot. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Lucky_Blocks | id=B5-0365 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-09-17 | checked=2026-11-07]
The Admin Lucky Block, Los Lucky Blocks, Taco Lucky Block and Los Taco Blocks in Steal a Brainrot can only be obtained when Sammy spawns them during Admin Abuse or Taco Tuesday. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Lucky_Blocks | id=B5-0366 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-09-17 | checked=2026-11-07]
Luck does not affect Lucky Blocks in Steal a Brainrot, because the Brainrot inside is decided when the block first spawns. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Lucky_Blocks | id=B5-0367 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-09-17 | checked=2026-11-07]
On February 6, 2026 at 12:52 PM, Sammy announced on Discord that Cerberus would not be replaced, and that new Brainrots would be added to the Mythic, Brainrot God and Secret Lucky Blocks. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Lucky_Blocks | id=B5-0368 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-09-17 | event=2026-02-06 | checked=2026-11-07]
Each seasonal Lucky Block in Steal a Brainrot has its own rarity: Spooky, Festive, Valentine's for the Heart Lucky Block, St. Patrick's for the Leprechaun Lucky Block, and Easter for the Egg Lucky Block. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Lucky_Blocks | id=B5-0369 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-09-17 | checked=2026-11-07]
Brainrot God Lucky Block is the longest Lucky Block name in Steal a Brainrot, at 21 characters. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Lucky_Blocks | id=B5-0371 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-09-17 | checked=2026-11-07]
The Secret, Mythic and Brainrot God Lucky Blocks were the only Lucky Blocks in Steal a Brainrot with timers, until Update 62 made every Lucky Block instantly openable. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Lucky_Blocks | id=B5-0372 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-09-17 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Update 62 change per the wiki: now every lucky Block can be insta-opened.]
### Lumaca Malefica
Lumaca Malefica is based on Snailenzo and is the second Brainrot in Steal a Brainrot based on a seasonal Fuse Machine, the Witch Fuse, and the first of these not in the Buho Family. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Lumaca_Malefica | id=B5-0373 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-03 | checked=2026-11-07]
Lumaca Malefica wears a witch hat in Steal a Brainrot, even though it is not from the Witch Fuse. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Lumaca_Malefica | id=B5-0374 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-03 | checked=2026-11-07]
Lumaca Malefica is a direct Italian translation of Maleficent Snail in Steal a Brainrot, one of few Brainrots whose Italian name is not written in brainrot Italian. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Lumaca_Malefica | id=B5-0375 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-03 | checked=2026-11-07]
Lumaca Malefica in Steal a Brainrot has the same color and anatomy as Snailenzo, but without the car part. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Lumaca_Malefica | id=B5-0376 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-03 | checked=2026-11-07]
Lumaca Malefica in Steal a Brainrot wears a black witch hat with a purple ribbon and a crescent moon accessory on its shell, and holds a magic staff. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Lumaca_Malefica | id=B5-0377 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-03 | checked=2026-11-07]

Teaser name missing from the text.]
Luv Luv Luv in Steal a Brainrot has covered-up makeup on its face and a side ponytail with a pink ribbon. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Luv_Luv_Luv | id=B5-0381 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-05 | checked=2026-11-07]

### Malame Amarele
Malame Amarele in Steal a Brainrot was added on September 6, 2025 in the Craft Machine update. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Malame_Amarele | id=B5-0384 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-09-05 | event=2025-09-06 | checked=2026-11-07]

[source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Malame_Amarele | id=B5-0387 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-09-05 | checked=2026-11-07]

Malame Amarele in Steal a Brainrot was created by ofuscabreno, according to the infobox. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Malame_Amarele | id=B5-0389 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=high | pub=2026-09-05 | checked=2026-11-07]

### Matteo
Matteo is the first human Brainrot in Steal a Brainrot, and Antonio is the second. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Matteo | id=B5-0409 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-02 | checked=2026-11-07]
Matteo in Steal a Brainrot has an actual human name, which is translated to Matthew. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Matteo | id=B5-0410 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-02 | checked=2026-11-07]
Matteo in Steal a Brainrot has 4 reskins, tied with Tralalero Tralala for second most, while La Grande Combinasion has the most with 8. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Matteo | id=B5-0411 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-02 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=The subject is blank in the wiki text. Matteo is inferred from the page.]
Matteo's ritual in Steal a Brainrot needs 3 players holding Matteo on top of each other, and it spawns Los Matteos with the Matteo event that can give the Hat trait. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Matteo | id=B5-0412 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-02 | checked=2026-11-07]
Matteo is the only Brainrot in Steal a Brainrot whose ritual uses a vertical formation instead of the usual horizontal one. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Matteo | id=B5-0413 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-02 | checked=2026-11-07]
Matteo's seasonal counterparts in Steal a Brainrot are Frankentteo at Halloween, Santteo at Christmas, Patteo at St. Patrick's and Buntteo at Easter. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Matteo | id=B5-0414 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-02 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=The Halloween, St. Patrick's and Easter counterparts are in the same trivia list.]
The seasonal counterpart pattern for Matteo in Steal a Brainrot stopped in the summer. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Matteo | id=B5-0415 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-02 | checked=2026-11-07]
Trees grow on the map in Steal a Brainrot before Matteo spawns, and Rainbow trees guarantee the spawned Matteo is Rainbow. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Matteo | id=B5-0416 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-02 | checked=2026-11-07]
Matteo has the only spawn effect in Steal a Brainrot that shouts its name as the sound. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Matteo | id=B5-0417 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-02 | checked=2026-11-07]
Matteo in Steal a Brainrot can be obtained during Admin Abuse, from the Backrooms Event, or by rolling from the RNG Machine. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Matteo | id=B5-0418 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-02 | checked=2026-11-07]
Matteo in Steal a Brainrot was created by @polonavale, according to the infobox. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Matteo | id=B5-0419 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=high | pub=2026-11-02 | checked=2026-11-07]

### Meowl
Meowl is currently the second-best Brainrot obtainable through normal gameplay in Steal a Brainrot, behind Strawberry Elephant and tied with Headless Horseman. Meowl in Steal a Brainrot was buffed six times, from $275M/s to $300M/s, $400M/s, $450M/s, $500M/s and finally $600M/s, with its price also buffed. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Meowl | id=B5-0423 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-04 | checked=2026-11-07]
Meowl in Steal a Brainrot unlocks an Exclusive Base while it is in your base, and the base disappears if someone holds it. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Meowl | id=B5-0424 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-04 | checked=2026-11-07]
The name Meowl is a portmanteau of meow and owl in Steal a Brainrot. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Meowl | id=B5-0425 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-04 | checked=2026-11-07]
Meowl in Steal a Brainrot costs 1083 and a third times its income, which is the only Brainrot whose price is not 1000 times its income. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Meowl | id=B5-0426 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-04 | checked=2026-11-07]
Meowl is Sammy (SpyderSammy)'s and LocalNeer's favorite Brainrot in Steal a Brainrot. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Meowl | id=B5-0427 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-04 | checked=2026-11-07]
According to Sammy, the best mutation for Meowl in Steal a Brainrot is Cyber visually, and the best trait is Strawberry. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Meowl | id=B5-0428 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-04 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Sammy's statement as reported on the wiki. The trait part is in the same bullet.]
Meowl can be bought from the Red Carpet in Steal a Brainrot. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Meowl | id=B5-0429 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-04 | checked=2026-11-07]
Meowl in Steal a Brainrot can be crafted in the Cyber Craft Machine from 3 Noobini Pizzanini and 1 Headless Horseman, among other recipes. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Meowl | id=B5-0430 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-04 | checked=2026-11-07]
Meowl has green eyes in Steal a Brainrot. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Meowl | id=B5-0431 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-04 | checked=2026-11-07]

Mi Gatito in Steal a Brainrot was created by Princesita Kelly, according to the infobox. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Mi_Gatito | id=B5-0441 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=high | pub=2026-09-06 | checked=2026-11-07]
### Moby Bros
Moby Bros in Steal a Brainrot has the same exact stats as Love Love Bear. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Moby_Bros | id=B5-0452 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-07 | checked=2026-11-07]
Moby Bros can be crafted at the Los Traders in Steal a Brainrot from Jelly Moby and Los Puggies, from Jelly Moby and Sammyni Cakini, or from Jelly Moby and Los Tictacs. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Moby_Bros | id=B5-0453 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-07 | checked=2026-11-07]
### Money Money Bros
Money Money Bros was teased by Sammy (SpyderSammy) in Steal a Brainrot. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Money_Money_Bros | id=B5-0454 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=The place of the tease is blank in the wiki text.]
Money Money Bros in Steal a Brainrot is the first time the baby version of Money Money Reindeer is shown. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Money_Money_Bros | id=B5-0455 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Only one of the Money Money Bros in Steal a Brainrot has a baby version of itself, which is the baby Money Money Puggy. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Money_Money_Bros | id=B5-0456 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
The Money Money Puggy and Money Money Reindeer together would yield $46M/s in Steal a Brainrot, only $1M/s less than their original income. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Money_Money_Bros | id=B5-0457 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
The baby Money Money Puggy in Money Money Bros in Steal a Brainrot uses the model taken from Los Puggies. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Money_Money_Bros | id=B5-0458 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Money Money Bros can be crafted in the Cyber Craft Machine in Steal a Brainrot from 1 Money Money Puggy and 1 Money Money Reindeer. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Money_Money_Bros | id=B5-0459 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
### Money Money Cat
Money Money Cat in Steal a Brainrot is a pixelated black cat with wide, golden-rimmed eyes and a tiny pink nose. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Money_Money_Cat | id=B5-0460 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-07 | checked=2026-11-07]
Money Money Cat in Steal a Brainrot has a cluster of banknotes bound tightly to its raised, curling tail. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Money_Money_Cat | id=B5-0461 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-07 | checked=2026-11-07]

Money Money Cat in Steal a Brainrot has the same stats as Gattino Hydrantino. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Money_Money_Cat | id=B5-0463 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-07 | checked=2026-11-07]
Sammy gave players a code to redeem Money Money Cat in Steal a Brainrot when it was added. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Money_Money_Cat | id=B5-0464 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-07 | checked=2026-11-07]
### Money Money Man
Money Money Man in Steal a Brainrot was added on November 8, 2025 at 3:00 PM EST. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Money_Money_Man | id=B5-0465 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-02 | event=2025-11-08 | checked=2026-11-07]

Money Money Man is the only money Brainrot in Steal a Brainrot that is a Brainrot God, while the other money Brainrots are Secret.
