Money Money Man in Steal a Brainrot has a golden monocle, a mustache and a gold walking cane. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Money_Money_Man | id=B5-0470 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-02 | checked=2026-11-07]
### Money Money Puggy
Money Money Puggy in Steal a Brainrot was released on September 27, 2025. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Money_Money_Puggy | id=B6-0001 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-31 | event=2025-09-27 | checked=2026-11-07]
Money Money Puggy in Steal a Brainrot was originally called Money Muh Money Money. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Money_Money_Puggy | id=B6-0002 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-31 | checked=2026-11-07]
Money Money Puggy in Steal a Brainrot was first released with its eyes facing a different angle, and they were later changed to face forward. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Money_Money_Puggy | id=B6-0003 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-31 | checked=2026-11-07]
Money Money Puggy in Steal a Brainrot has ears made of dollar bills, a gold collar, gold straps and gold coins on its cheeks. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Money_Money_Puggy | id=B6-0004 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-31 | checked=2026-11-07]
Money Money Puggy in Steal a Brainrot has the same stats as Churrito Bunnito. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Money_Money_Puggy | id=B6-0005 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-31 | checked=2026-11-07]
Two Money Money Puggys placed facing each other at the front corners of the Robux Shop perform the Money Money Puggy Ritual in Steal a Brainrot, which spawns Los Puggies and activates the Money Event. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Money_Money_Puggy | id=B6-0006 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-31 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Wiki wording says Line 2 Money Money Puggys; the layout was unclear.]
Money Money Puggy in Steal a Brainrot can be obtained from the Red Carpet, from Sammy's Base with a relatively low chance, from the RNG Machine, or from codes. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Money_Money_Puggy | id=B6-0008 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-31 | checked=2026-11-07]
Los Puggies in Steal a Brainrot were a Brainrot Dealer stock item before becoming trade-exclusive through the Brainrot Trader. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Money_Money_Puggy | id=B6-0009 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-31 | checked=2026-11-07]
Money Money Puggy in Steal a Brainrot was supposed to get a variant called Money Meow, which was scrapped and replaced with Los Puggies. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Money_Money_Puggy | id=B6-0010 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-31 | checked=2026-11-07]
### Money Money Reindeer
Money Money Reindeer in Steal a Brainrot costs the same as Nuclearo Dinossauro, $2.5B, but makes $10M/s more than Nuclearo Dinossauro. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Money_Money_Reindeer | id=B6-0012 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-04 | checked=2026-11-07]

Money Money Reindeer in Steal a Brainrot has antlers decorated with lights and two stars on ropes, a torso covered in money stripes and coins, and money stripes on its legs and ears. Money Money Reindeer in Steal a Brainrot can be obtained in the Gingerbread Town event with a small spawn chance, or bought from Santa's Shop for Gold Elves or Robux. Naughty Naughty in Steal a Brainrot has green boots and gloves and holds a green present box with coal inside. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Naughty_Naughty | id=B6-0045 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-11 | checked=2026-11-07]
### Nerf
Raccooni Jandelini in Steal a Brainrot was secretly nerfed from $14/s to $12/s for unknown reasons. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Raccooni_Jandelini | id=B7-0034 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-07 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Nerf date not given on the wiki.]
### Noobini Pizzanini
Los Noobinis, the Los version of Noobini Pizzanini in Steal a Brainrot, were obtained from the Craft Machine, Cyber Craft and RNG Machine before those machines were removed. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Noobini_Pizzanini | id=B6-0090 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-08 | checked=2026-11-07]
Noobini Pizzanini in Steal a Brainrot has the shortest break-even point of any Brainrot, taking 25 seconds at 1x multiplier. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Noobini_Pizzanini | id=B6-0091 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-08 | checked=2026-11-07]
Noobini Pizzanini is the only Brainrot in Steal a Brainrot unaffected by the Sleepy trait, because its income of $0.5/s is rounded up to $1/s. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Noobini_Pizzanini | id=B6-0092 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-08 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Explanation is from the wiki's rounding logic.]
Noobini Pizzanini in Steal a Brainrot gets no income boost from the Gold mutation, since $1.25/s is rounded down to $1/s. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Noobini_Pizzanini | id=B6-0093 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-08 | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot, if a player has never bought a Noobini Pizzanini, the game shows an arrow pointing to one when it spawns, with the message Go buy a Noobini Pizzanini. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Noobini_Pizzanini | id=B6-0094 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-08 | checked=2026-11-07]
Noobini Santanini is the only reskin of Noobini Pizzanini in Steal a Brainrot, not counting the Pipi Family. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Noobini_Pizzanini | id=B6-0095 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-08 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Wiki says first and only with a blank category word; the claim conflicts with many other reskins, so it is probably Common-only.]
Noobini Pizzanini and Pipi Corni are the only Common Brainrots in Steal a Brainrot to get a Los version. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Noobini_Pizzanini | id=B6-0096 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-08 | checked=2026-11-07]
Noobini Pizzanini's name combines Noob, a Roblox term for a new or unskilled player, with pizza. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Noobini_Pizzanini | id=B6-0097 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-08 | checked=2026-11-07]
### Noobini Santanini
Noobini Santanini in Steal a Brainrot is slightly bigger than Noobini Pizzanini, has studs on its arms, legs and head, and has a more dynamic walk. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Noobini_Santanini | id=B6-0099 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
### Noodle Noodle Poodle
Noodle Noodle Poodle in Steal a Brainrot has the same stats as Tralaledon and Globa Steppa, and the same income as Gobblino Uniciclino. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Noodle_Noodle_Poodle | id=B6-0100 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-07 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Income match to Gobblino Uniciclino is from the same trivia block.]
Noodle Noodle Poodle is the fourth Money Brainrot in Steal a Brainrot, after Money Money Puggy, Money Money Reindeer and Love Love Bear. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Noodle_Noodle_Poodle | id=B6-0101 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-07 | checked=2026-11-07]
Noodle Noodle Poodle in Steal a Brainrot has a blue whistle necklace and a yellow band of rolled noodles in pink, orange, purple and green. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Noodle_Noodle_Poodle | id=B6-0102 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-07 | checked=2026-11-07]

Noo La Polizia in Steal a Brainrot is Los Nooo My Hotspotsitos in police uniforms, with the middle one holding a walkie-talkie, the left one holding handcuffs and a baton, and the right one holding a flashlight and notebook. ### Noo my Eggs
Noo my Eggs in Steal a Brainrot was the only Easter Hour Brainrot used in the La Easter Grande recipe. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Noo_my_Eggs | id=B6-0061 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]

When Sammy tried to buff Noo my Examen in Steal a Brainrot, he accidentally buffed Noo my Present instead, and this was later fixed. Noo my Examen in Steal a Brainrot has a red pencil with a blue end and blue sneakers. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Noo_my_Examen | id=B6-0073 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-16 | checked=2026-11-07]

[source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Pinealotto_Fruttarino | id=B6-0250 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-11 | checked=2026-11-07]
Pinealotto Fruttarino in Steal a Brainrot was introduced in the October 11, 2025 update. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Pinealotto_Fruttarino | id=B6-0251 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-11 | event=2025-10-11 | checked=2026-11-07]
Pinealotto Fruttarino in Steal a Brainrot has green gills sprouting from both sides of its head and one from each hand. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Pinealotto_Fruttarino | id=B6-0252 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-11 | checked=2026-11-07]

Pineaplino in Steal a Brainrot has the same stats as Ballerino Lololo, making it the DLC Brainrot with the lowest income. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Pineaplino | id=B6-0255 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-02 | checked=2026-11-07]
Pineaplino in Steal a Brainrot has plant-like eyebrows, sunglasses, 4-toed feet and a swag expression. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Pineaplino | id=B6-0256 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-02 | checked=2026-11-07]

Pin Pin Pengu in Steal a Brainrot is a voxel-style penguin with brown boots. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Pin_Pin_Pengu | id=B6-0249 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-31 | checked=2026-11-07]

Pipi Avocado is the third highest earning Rare Brainrot in Steal a Brainrot, behind Pinealotto Fruttarino and Pengolino Nuvoletto. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Pipi_Avocado | id=B6-0258 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-09-30 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Category word is blank; ranking is among Rare Brainrots.]
Sammy (SpyderSammy) kept adding Pipi Avocado to upcoming Fuse Machines in Steal a Brainrot, so it did not become rare after the Fuse was gone. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Pipi_Avocado | id=B6-0259 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-09-30 | checked=2026-11-07]
### Pipi Corni
Pipi Corni in Steal a Brainrot was the first Brainrot to come from a Fuse Machine, according to the wiki. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Pipi_Corni | id=B6-0260 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-25 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Conflicts with the Pipi Avocado page claim.]
Pipi Corni in Steal a Brainrot is the first Brainrot to not come from the Red Carpet. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Pipi_Corni | id=B6-0261 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-25 | checked=2026-11-07]
The value of Pipi Corni in Steal a Brainrot fell after the 2026 Fuse Machine returned, and fell further when it was reintroduced in the Summer Fuse. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Pipi_Corni | id=B6-0262 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-25 | checked=2026-11-07]
Pipi Corni is used in a recipe to craft Los Cornis at the Los Traders in Steal a Brainrot. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Pipi_Corni | id=B6-0263 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-25 | checked=2026-11-07]
Several Pipi Corni mutations in Steal a Brainrot have fewer than 10,000 existing, including Candy, Lava and Radioactive. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Pipi_Corni | id=B6-0264 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-25 | checked=2026-11-07]
Pipi Corni and other fuse Brainrots were brought back twice in Steal a Brainrot, in the Fuse Machine and the Summer Fuse. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Pipi_Corni | id=B6-0265 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-25 | checked=2026-11-07]
Pipi Corni in Steal a Brainrot is a dormouse with a ':3' face. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Pipi_Corni | id=B6-0266 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-25 | checked=2026-11-07]
### Pipi Kiwi
Pipi Kiwi is the first Pipi Brainrot in the Index of Steal a Brainrot. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Pipi_Kiwi | id=B6-0267 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-09-13 | checked=2026-11-07]
The word pipi in the Pipi Kiwi name in Steal a Brainrot is a Maori word meaning baby or infant. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Pipi_Kiwi | id=B6-0268 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-09-13 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Te reo spelling is macron-marked in the source; the Maori word is written as in the source.]
Pipi Kiwi with mutations or traits in Steal a Brainrot has a 15% chance to pass them on in the Fuse Machine, the highest inherit chance for Common Brainrots. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Pipi_Kiwi | id=B6-0269 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-09-13 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Wiki says this is the highest inherit chance for its rarity's top-income Brainrot.]

### Pot Pumpkin
Pot Pumpkin in Steal a Brainrot has a darker skeleton, a flat jack-o'-lantern face and holds a chocolate bar. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Pot_Pumpkin | id=B6-0329 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Pot Pumpkin is the second Brainrot that can be dug up in the Grave Digger Event in Steal a Brainrot, after Skull Skull Skull. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Pot_Pumpkin | id=B6-0330 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
In Steal a Brainrot, digging up Pot Pumpkin with a full base sends it to the Red Carpet instead. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Pot_Pumpkin | id=B6-0331 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Pot Pumpkin does not appear on the Escape Tsunami LTM in Steal a Brainrot, unlike Skull Skull Skull. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Pot_Pumpkin | id=B6-0332 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Pot Pumpkin can appear in a house during the Trick or Treating event in Steal a Brainrot and gives 30 Candy Corns. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Pot_Pumpkin | id=B6-0333 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
### Prediction
The name Rosetti Tualetti in Steal a Brainrot was predicted by MothPastryy. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Rosetti_Tualetti | id=B7-0102 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
### Pretzo Robo
Pretzo Robo's former name in Steal a Brainrot was Pretzel Bot 3000. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Pretzo_Robo | id=B6-0334 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-19 | checked=2026-11-07]
Sammy (SpyderSammy) buffed Pretzo Robo in Steal a Brainrot in Update 71. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Pretzo_Robo | id=B6-0335 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-19 | checked=2026-11-07]
Before its buff, Pretzo Robo in Steal a Brainrot made $5K/s more than Jackorilla, the worst Brainrot. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Pretzo_Robo | id=B6-0336 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-19 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Category word is blank in the wiki.]
About 38,000 Pretzo Robo exist in Steal a Brainrot, because the craft needs Ginger Cisterna, a Santa's Fuse exclusive Brainrot. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Pretzo_Robo | id=B6-0337 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-19 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Exist count of around 38,000 is the wiki's confirmed-count claim.]
Sammy (SpyderSammy) confirmed in one Admin Abuse that more Money Money Bros had been crafted than Pretzo Robo in Steal a Brainrot. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Pretzo_Robo | id=B6-0338 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-19 | checked=2026-11-07]
Pretzo Robo in Steal a Brainrot has two antennas on its head and two crystal shards on its shoulder. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Pretzo_Robo | id=B6-0339 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-19 | checked=2026-11-07]

### Trenotubo Axolotrico 9000
Trenotubo Axolotrico 9000 in Steal a Brainrot says Nine Thousand instead of the usual Nueve Mila in its sound. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Trenotubo_Axolotrico_9000 | id=B8-0211 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-03 | checked=2026-11-07]
Trenotubo Axolotrico 9000 is the first Brainrot in Steal a Brainrot to have a 3 second TTS sound. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Trenotubo_Axolotrico_9000 | id=B8-0212 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-03 | checked=2026-11-07]
The name of Trenotubo Axolotrico 9000 in Steal a Brainrot is probably a misspelling of Trenoturbo Axolotrico 9000, missing an R. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Trenotubo_Axolotrico_9000 | id=B8-0214 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-03 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=The wiki says probably; the spelling is kept as Trenotubo because of its tube shape.]
Trenotubo Axolotrico 9000 in Steal a Brainrot is crafted in the Cyber Craft Machine from Trenostruzzo Turbo 3000, Matteo and Tigroligre Frutonni. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Trenotubo_Axolotrico_9000 | id=B8-0215 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-03 | checked=2026-11-07]
After Matteo became obtainable again in the Backrooms Event, Trenotubo Axolotrico 9000 in Steal a Brainrot became the easiest Brainrot God to make. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Trenotubo_Axolotrico_9000 | id=B8-0216 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-03 | checked=2026-11-07 | note=Wiki says it is possibly the easiest Cyber Craft Machine Brainrot too.]
Trenotubo Axolotrico 9000 in Steal a Brainrot is an axolotl with a subway train torso and a robotic mech. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Trenotubo_Axolotrico_9000 | id=B8-0217 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-03 | checked=2026-11-07]
### Trickolino
The original name of Trickolino in Steal a Brainrot was Il Tomenoso Chachechi. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Trickolino | id=B8-0221 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Trickolino's sign in Steal a Brainrot is based on a famous Halloween trick-or-treat bowl sign that allows only one piece of candy. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Trickolino | id=B8-0222 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Trickolino in Steal a Brainrot has the highest chance of flinging you back in Trick or Treat, and gives the least Candy Corn, by only 20 Candy Corn. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Trickolino | id=B8-0223 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Trickolino in Steal a Brainrot has a sign reading TAKE ONLY ONE! and has Halloween lights in its body. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Trickolino | id=B8-0224 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
### Tric Trac Baraboom
Tric Trac Baraboom in Steal a Brainrot has almost identical animations to Cacto Hipopotamo. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Tric_Trac_Baraboom | id=B8-0218 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-09-30 | checked=2026-11-07]
Tric Trac Baraboom in Steal a Brainrot has ears that look like zucchini leaves on its giant zucchini body. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Tric_Trac_Baraboom | id=B8-0219 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-09-30 | checked=2026-11-07]
Tric Trac Baraboom in Steal a Brainrot was created by @__chenesacc__ and @reisonbs, according to its infobox. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Tric_Trac_Baraboom | id=B8-0220 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-09-30 | checked=2026-11-07]
### Triplito Tralaleritos
Triplito Tralaleritos in Steal a Brainrot was added in Update 29. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Triplito_Tralaleritos | id=B8-0226 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Triplito Tralaleritos is the only Brainrot in the Festive Lucky Block in Steal a Brainrot that is not related to Christmas. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Triplito_Tralaleritos | id=B8-0227 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Triplito Tralaleritos is the only Los Brainrot in Steal a Brainrot that does not start with Los. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Triplito_Tralaleritos | id=B8-0228 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
Triplito Tralaleritos in Steal a Brainrot stacks three Los Tralaleritos, with a happy top one in a face disguise and hat, a sad crying middle one and an angry bottom one. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Triplito_Tralaleritos | id=B8-0229 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-01 | checked=2026-11-07]
### Trippi Troppi
Trippi Troppi is the first Brainrot in the Index in Steal a Brainrot, meaning it is the cheapest one. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Trippi_Troppi | id=B8-0230 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-23 | checked=2026-11-07]
The cat-shrimp Trippi Troppi was the first version added to Steal a Brainrot, in Update 01. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Trippi_Troppi | id=B8-0231 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-23 | checked=2026-11-07]
The fish-bear version of Trippi Troppi was added later to Steal a Brainrot under the name Trippi Troppi Troppa Trippa. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Trippi_Troppi | id=B8-0232 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-23 | checked=2026-11-07]
Trippi Troppi in Steal a Brainrot could be obtained by Fishing, as it is in the Aquatic Index. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Trippi_Troppi | id=B8-0233 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-23 | checked=2026-11-07]
Trippi Troppi is one of the Rebirth 1 requirements in Steal a Brainrot, along with Gangster Footera (formerly Tung Tung Tung Sahur). [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Trippi_Troppi | id=B8-0234 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-10-23 | checked=2026-11-07]
### Trippi Troppi Troppa Trippa
Trippi Troppi Troppa Trippa in Steal a Brainrot was created by @1raidex_, according to its infobox. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Trippi_Troppi_Troppa_Trippa | id=B8-0235 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-02 | checked=2026-11-07]
Trippi Troppi Troppa Trippa in Steal a Brainrot can be bought from the Red Carpet or fished from the Fishing Event. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Trippi_Troppi_Troppa_Trippa | id=B8-0236 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-02 | checked=2026-11-07]
Trippi Troppi Troppa Trippa was the first Brainrot in Steal a Brainrot to have two separate versions. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Trippi_Troppi_Troppa_Trippa | id=B8-0237 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-02 | checked=2026-11-07]
Some players call Trippi Troppi Troppa Trippa in Steal a Brainrot Troppa Trippa to avoid confusion with Trippi Troppi. [source: https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Trippi_Troppi_Troppa_Trippa | id=B8-0238 | type=community | status=unverified | confidence=medium | pub=2026-11-02 | checked=2026-11-07]

[source: https://techwiser.com/roblox-steal-a-brainrot-codes/ | id=A07-0009 | checked=2026-11-06]

API (fetched 2026-11-06, record updated 2026-08-08): 375 Robux. Wiki Robux Shop (page last edited 2026-09-06) and wiki Gamepasses and Dev Products page (last edited 2026-09-29) list 499 Robux. The API is the current value; the wiki figure may be stale. [source: https://apis.roblox.com/game-passes/v1/universes/7709344486/game-passes?passView=Full&pageSize=100 | id=A08-0002 | checked=2026-11-06]
# Conflict - Admin Panel gamepass: Sources disagree on the Robux price of the Admin Panel in Steal a Brainrot: the Roblox game-passes API shows 7,999 under the name Admin Commands, the wiki Robux Shop shows 7,499, and the wiki Gamepasses page shows 9,999. API (fetched 2026-11-06, record updated 2026-08-08) matches the Admin Panel by its description, which is the ;cmds command list. # Conflict - Steal a Brainrot: Sources disagree on how many concurrent players Steal a Brainrot had on August 23, 2025: PocketGamer.biz, citing Offpath data, says 20 million, while IGN, citing Fortnite.gg data, says 15 million. PocketGamer.biz (2025-08-27) relays a LinkedIn post by Roblox strategy consultant James Purell that uses Offpath data, giving 20 million for Steal a Brainrot and 21.1 million for Grow a Garden. Dexerto (2025-08-25) repeats the IGN numbers. Wikipedia says 20 million and cites IGN, but the IGN text gives 15 million. Roblox's letter gives no per-game figure. Neither number is official. [source: https://www.ign.com/articles/roblox-hits-fresh-player-record-towering-over-steam-and-fortnite-amid-war-between-its-two-most-popular-games-grow-a-garden-and-steal-a-brainrot | id=A16-0005 | checked=2026-11-06]
# Conflict - Roblox: Tracker figures for Roblox's platform peak on August 23, 2025 differ: Dexerto says 47.3 million and PocketGamer.biz says 47.4 million, while Roblox's own letter says over 45 million. Dexerto's 47.3 million matches the Fortnite.gg-based figure in IGN (2025-08-26), which says 47 million. PocketGamer's 47.4 million relays the Offpath-based post. Wikipedia uses 47.4 million and cites PocketGamer.biz. [source: https://www.dexerto.com/roblox/roblox-smashes-concurrent-user-record-thanks-to-war-between-two-games-3242035/ | id=A16-0006 | checked=2026-11-06]
# Conflict - Steal a Brainrot: Sources disagree on Steal a Brainrot's September 2025 peak: Dexerto says the Roblox version reached 23.4 million, its 24 million headline adds the Fortnite version, and Wikipedia and PocketGamer.biz give 24 million and 24.1 million. Dexerto dates the 23.4 million figure to September 14 in its text, but the embedded post by community account ShiinaBR is dated September 13, 2025. Dexerto's 542,000 is from the separate Fortnite Creative version, so do not read 24 million as a Roblox-only figure. Wikipedia dates its 24 million to September 13 and cites Gaming News, which I could not open. PocketGamer.biz's 24.1 million has no source given. [source: https://www.dexerto.com/gaming/steal-a-brainrot-smashes-records-with-nearly-24-million-players-across-roblox-and-fortnite-3250973/ | id=A16-0007 | checked=2026-11-06]
# Conflict - Grow a Garden: Sources disagree on Grow a Garden's peak on August 23, 2025: IGN, citing Fortnite.gg data, says 22 million; Wikipedia says at least 22.3 million; PocketGamer.biz, citing Offpath data, says 21.1 million. Roblox's letter says Grow a Garden set a record of nearly 22 million in July 2025, and PocketGamer.biz gives 21.3 million for June. The dates and numbers differ across these sources. [source: https://www.ign.com/articles/roblox-hits-fresh-player-record-towering-over-steam-and-fortnite-amid-war-between-its-two-most-popular-games-grow-a-garden-and-steal-a-brainrot | id=A16-0026 | checked=2026-11-06]

The Steal a Brainrot wiki says Smurf Cat was created by artist Nate Hallinan in 2014 and posted on his own website (https://stealabrainrot.fandom.com/wiki/Smurf_Cat). Know Your Meme says the meme began on the Russian-speaking internet under the name Shailushai and gained popularity on TikTok in August 2023 (https://knowyourmeme.com/memes/smurf-cat). Know Your Meme's page says it was posted to worth1000 in July 2007 (https://knowyourmeme.com/memes/strawberry-elephant).
